title: Hypotension Prediction Index versus High Mean Arterial Pressure Target for Preventing Intraoperative Hypotension: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: The Hypotension Prediction Index (HPI) was developed to predict intraoperative hypotension several minutes before its occurrence. Although previous randomized trials reported reduced hypotension with HPI-guided management, these findings may partly reflect performance bias from open-label designs and selection bias in algorithm validation. Recent observational evidence suggests that much of HPI’s apparent benefit may result from earlier treatment at higher mean arterial pressure (MAP) thresholds, supporting direct randomized comparison with a proactive higher MAP target. Methods: In this open-label, parallel-group randomized controlled trial at two centers, 100 adults undergoing major noncardiac surgery requiring invasive arterial monitoring were equally randomized to HPI-guided management (treatment triggered when HPI greater than or equal to 85) or a higher MAP–targeted strategy (treatment triggered when MAP less than or equal to 73 mmHg), both following the same predefined hemodynamic protocol. The primary endpoint was time-weighted average hypotension (MAP less than 65 mmHg), used to test superiority of HPI-guided management over a proactive higher MAP target. Secondary outcomes included area under the threshold for hypotension, hypertension burden (MAP greater than 100 mmHg), norepinephrine dose, length of hospital stay, and 30-day mortality. title: Strategic learning as a catalyst: unveiling the impact of market and customer orientation on firm performance in the technology sector
abstract: Purpose For strategic learning (SL) to be successful, the dissemination of information within the company must be clear and concise. For this purpose, the study aims to examine how market orientation (MO) and customer orientation (CO) affect SL and therefore how SL affects firm strategies (FS) and firm performance (FP). Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was used using a structured survey based on an extensive literature review. To improve the questionnaire, a pretest was conducted with 62 managers (excluded from the final sample). The survey was applied to 460 managers in information technology (IT) Companies in Istanbul. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS 25, LISREL and IBM SPSS Process V3 plug-in for mediation effect analysis. The survey was designed to avoid common method variance by ensuring anonymity and appropriate response times. Findings Analysis results reveal that MO and CO positively affect SL. SL positively affects FS and FP. In addition, SL mediates the relationships between MO and FS, MO and FP, CO and FS and CO and FP. Research limitations/implications The fact that the research is limited to IT companies in Istanbul may affect the generalizability of the findings. Future research may expand the scope to other sectors and regions to confirm the results. In addition, the use of cross-sectional data limits the capability to make causal inferences, …

title: A study on efficiency dynamics of equity options market: evidence from national stock exchange, India
abstract: Purpose The study aims to investigate the efficiency dynamics of the single stock equity options market concerning the National Stock Exchange (NSE), India. Design/methodology/approach This study examines the efficiency of the single stock equity call options market over 110 months from January 2011 to February 2020 by analyzing violations of the lower boundary condition (LBC) and arbitrage profit thereof. The authors use the runs test and the test of proportions to assess market efficiency and use binary logistic regression to identify and examine the relationship between LBC violation and its significant explanatory variables. Findings The analysis reveals trends in LBC violations for the entire sample of equity stock options, indicating market inefficiency. Additionally, the study shows that a bullish underlying spot market, shorter time to expiry and lower trading volume of equity stock options contracts increase the likelihood of LBC violations and arbitrage profits, ignoring transaction costs. Practical implication – Overall, the findings intend to forecast arbitrage trading opportunities by identifying significant explanatory variables and their impact, thereby contributing to market efficiency. Practical implications Overall, the findings intend to forecast arbitrage trading opportunities by identifying significant explanatory variables and their impact, thereby contrib…

title: Research on the Impact Mechanism of the Fusion Model on Stock Valuation Correction and Market Risk Forecasting in an Uncertain Environment
abstract: Under geopolitical tensions and monetary policy shifts, global stock market volatility has intensified. Traditional valuation models and risk forecasting models, relying on historical static parameters and overlooking non-quantitative information such as management tone, suffer from systematic biases. This study uses the Chinese financial language model SilverSight and its ASSL framework as the core information-extraction tool and builds a fusion model. The integrated framework reconstructs asset pricing logic via a three-tier mechanism: extracting three types of complementary signals via ASSL, embedding them into DCF and GARCH-X as time-varying adjustments, and constructing a simultaneous equation system to reveal synergistic effects. Theoretical analysis indicates that the proposed framework transcends the conventional reliance on structured quantitative data and improves the accuracy of stock intrinsic value estimation and the forward-lovingness of market volatility forecasting through text-enhanced dynamic parameter adjustment. This study contributes a novel methodological pathway for the deep integration of large language models with asset pricing theory under uncertainty and a theoretical foundation for investors to leverage Chinese financial LLMs to enhance firm valuation and risk assessment.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Dynamic Pricing of Credit Derivatives under Market Uncertainty: A Default-Risk Adjustment Model
abstract: The static pricing model of credit default swaps (CDS) may not reflect the actual changes in the market due to capital flows and geopolitical conflicts at present, and thus will have a large valuation error. This paper extends a simplified reduced-form model by adding a Knightian uncertainty index to a jump-diffusion model of the default intensity and then builds a CDS pricing model with dynamic evolution of default risk. No-arbitrage pricing is used to find the equilibrium CDS spread, and the transmission from Knightian uncertainty to default intensity, expected default losses and CDS spread is explained. Based on the above theoretical analysis, a higher level of uncertainty will lead to a higher long-run default intensity, an increased expected loss from default, and thus a wider CDS spread. As the analysis is theoretical, the results of the reduction in pricing errors by the model should be regarded as a hypothesis. The following research will focus on the calibration and testing of the model with market data.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Labor Under Strain: The Latin American Right and the Politics of Market Reform
abstract: Abstract What explains differences in labor market reforms among conservative governments in Latin America during the 2010s–20s? Analyzing the 2000s “pink tide” as a critical juncture, we argue that two policy legacies account for this cross-national variation. First, the degree of labor movement empowerment under leftist governments conditioned whether subsequent conservative administrations pursued radical or more moderate reforms. Second, labor movement cohesion—shaped by the encompassment of confederations, partisan alignments, and bargaining institutions—determined whether governments pursued inequitable (targeting specific segments of the workforce) or equitable reforms. We analyze the administrations of Temer and Bolsonaro in Brazil, Macri and Milei in Argentina, and Lacalle Pou in Uruguay. Our main contributions are to examine the seldom-explored distributional equity of austerity reforms in Latin America, demonstrating that under conditions of acute fiscal stress the public–private divide becomes a central dimension of labor market reform, and to introduce labor movement cohesion as a new explanatory variable in labor policy analysis.

title: Derivative Pricing under Uncertain Market Conditions: An Integrated Stochastic Volatility and Jump Framework
abstract: With the increase in uncertainty of the modern financial market, so too has the problem of derivative pricing risen. Traditionally, the Black-Scholes model has been a solid theoretical model. However, it relies on idealized assumptions such as constant volatility and continuous asset price movements. I In reality, financial markets do not always conform to this classical model; instead, they exhibit time-varying volatility, heavy-tailed return distributions, and sudden price changes. Therefore, the old derivative pricing models have obvious shortcomings. This paper introduces an integrated framework for derivative pricing under uncertain market conditions. By adding stochastic volatility and jump risks to the model, it better reflects fluctuations in asset prices than a traditional diffusion model. Based on the above analysis, the value of derivatives is closely linked to the distribution of future asset prices, and this distribution is determined by expected returns, fluctuations in volatility and tail risks. This framework contributes to existing derivative pricing literature by integrating two major sources of uncertainty that are often modeled separately. Furthermore, the model provides practical implications for risk management and derivative valuation, particularly during periods of growing market uncertainty.

Correlation between circulating tumor cell levels and tumor response in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma undergoing immunotherapy and molecular targeted therapy
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are closely associated with the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the clinical value of CTC detection in patients receiving systemic therapy for advanced HCC remains to be fully elucidated. A total of 125 patients with advanced HCC who underwent systemic therapy were enrolled in this study. Five milliliters of peripheral blood were collected at five time points: before treatment initiation, and 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after treatment. CTCs were isolated and captured using the Isolation by Size of Epithelial Tumor Cells (ISET) method. Tumor response to systemic treatment was evaluated according to the modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST). We further analyzed the correlation between dynamic changes in peripheral blood CTC levels and tumor response to systemic therapy. The overall objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were 39.2% (49/125) and 82.4% (103/125), respectively. Dynamic monitoring of CTCs revealed that CTC levels remained persistently high and gradually increased in patients with progressive disease (PD). In patients with complete response (CR) or partial response (PR), CTC levels decreased progressively during treatment and stayed at low levels thereafter. For patients with stable disease (SD), CTC counts began to decline 3 months after treatment but re…

title: Capital flight or speculative demand: asymmetric drivers of the crypto exchange rate premium in distressed zones
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the asymmetric determinants of the crypto exchange rate premiums in two distinct crisis contexts: Ukraine’s war economy and Argentina’s high-inflation regime. Design/methodology/approach This study employs the Nonlinear Autoregressive Distributed Lag model on monthly data from January 2020 to December 2024. Findings This study finds a significant divergence in the function of crypto assets across jurisdictions. In Ukraine, the crypto exchange rate premium functions as a war barometer, responding asymmetrically to geopolitical risk (GPR), trade uncertainty and macroeconomic sentiment. These findings support the capital flight hypothesis, with crypto serving as a crisis-driven channel for capital outflows. Conversely, Argentina’s premium is driven by inflation and trade uncertainty rather than political conflict, indicating that crypto primarily facilitates inflation hedging and financial arbitrage. Moreover, heightened global crypto price uncertainty dampens the premium in both countries, highlighting limits to crypto as a flight or speculative instrument. Practical implications By linking movements in the crypto premium to inflation, trade uncertainty, GPR, macroeconomic sentiment and global crypto volatility, this study sheds light on how digital assets interact with macroeconomic shocks, international financial frictions and reg…

title: From Surface Buffering to Bulk Ion Exchange: Mapping the Acid Response of Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) (K-PHI)
abstract: Abstract Potassium poly(heptazine imide) (K-PHI) is a promising material for photocatalysis and energy storage, yet its application in aqueous media is limited by protonation. Cation exchange to protonated poly(heptazine imide) (H-PHI) causes structural and optoelectronic changes. Herein, a systematic study of its acid stability regime and protonation threshold is presented through simultaneous consideration of PHI’s bulk, interface, and solution properties. Down to pH 3.0, solutions are buffered by proton adsorption while the particle bulk retains structural integrity, pointing to coexistence of H+ at the surface and K+ in the bulk. Within this regime down to pH 4.0, buffering coincides with a stable zeta potential, consistent with proton adsorption balanced by counterions. At yet lower pH, the buffer limit (pH 3.0) is characterized by surface destabilization, suggesting proton excess. At pH 2.0, protonation proceeds via bulk ion exchange and H-PHI formation.

Supply‑Demand Matching of Urban Community Sports Spaces in the Context of Gentrification: Evidence from Liwan District, Guangzhou
abstract: With the popularization of the national fitness concept and continuous urban renewal promotion, demographic and spatial function changes brought by gentrification reshape the supply demand relationship of community sports spaces. Taking Liwan District, Guangzhou as the case, this paper explores supply demand matching characteristics of urban community sports spaces under gentrification. The entropy weight method and the two step floating catchment area (2SFCA) method are adopted for empirical analysis. Results reveal obvious spatial differentiation of gentrification across Liwan District, with high gentrification zones concentrated in old city cores, historic cultural blocks and key urban renewal zones. Community sports spaces generally follow a supply pattern dominated by large scale public sports facilities and supplemented by small and micro sports venues. The overall supply demand matching presents spatial features of relative balance in central zones yet mismatch in partial high gentrification areas, while northern and southern fringes show low matching levels. This study introduces the gentrification perspective into community sports space supply demand matching research, and provides references for precise allocation and equitable use of public sports resources in high density old urban areas amid urban renewal.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Integrated multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and functional studies implicate MDK as a mediator of cisplatin-response phenotypes in ovarian cancer
abstract: Abstract Platinum resistance remains a central barrier to durable disease control in ovarian cancer. In this study, we integrated an ovarian cancer susceptibility GWAS, multi-omics profiling (CPTAC/TCGA), and spatial-single-cell transcriptomics to identify novel therapeutic targets. Cross-platform prioritization nominated midkine (MDK) as a prominent candidate associated with platinum-response phenotypes. Mapping of MDK via scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics localized its expression primarily to tumor-associated compartments, suggesting a critical role in microenvironmental remodeling. Clinically, in an expanded retrospective cohort of 138 patients, high MDK expression demonstrated a robust adjusted association with platinum resistance and poor overall survival, a finding further validated by propensity-score matching. Functionally, MDK depletion significantly attenuated malignant phenotypes and sensitized ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin in vitro , while strongly potentiating cisplatin-induced tumor suppression in in vivo xenograft models. Mechanistically, complementary in silico virtual perturbation analyses predicted a regulatory link between MDK and survival signaling networks. This was experimentally corroborated by bidirectional pharmacological rescue assays, which revealed that MDK drives cisplatin resistance primarily through the PI3K/AKT signaling axis, subsequentl…

title: Load increase response window identification and low-carbon regulation for grid-interactive salt lake chemical parks under process feasibility constraints
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy has intensified the pressure on power grids to accommodate renewable generation, while the production processes of energy intensive loads are subject to stringent process rigidity constraints, posing substantial challenges to source–load interactive scheduling. To address this issue, this paper investigates typical energy intensive loads in a salt lake chemical park and proposes a method for load increase response window identification and low-carbon regulation under process feasibility constraints. First, based on the material transfer relationships in potassium, lithium, and magnesium coproduction, a load increase potential assessment model is developed to characterize the formation and interprocess transfer of adjustable load potential by jointly considering process feasibility and distribution network access margins. Second, a feasibility discrimination model for load increase response windows is established, in which shift rhythm adaptation, material buffer consistency, and renewable power matching are incorporated into a unified evaluation framework. An improved method integrating the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) and multi-criteria optimization and compromise solution (VIKOR) is then used to identify suitable response windows under surplus renewable power conditions. Finally, a low-c…

title: Response to anti-VEGF injections for diabetic macular edema among patients on chronic exogenous insulin therapy
abstract: Abstract Purpose Diabetic macular edema (DME) is a leading cause of vision loss in diabetic patients worldwide. This study assessed whether there was a difference in functional and anatomic responsiveness to anti-VEGF therapy for DME among patients on chronic exogenous insulin therapy. Methods This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients diagnosed with DME between 2014 and 2022. Patients were divided into two groups: those who were treated with exogenous insulin and those who were not. Treatment characteristics such as the type and total number of anti-VEGF injections, the use of intravitreal or periocular steroids, and length of follow-up were recorded from patient charts. Functional and anatomic ocular characteristics were measured at baseline and six-month intervals up to 24 months from the time of DME diagnosis. The main outcome measures were change in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central foveal thickness (CFT), and macular volume (MV). Results 101 patients (148 eyes) met the criteria for inclusion in this study. 82 patients (81.2%) used insulin while 19 patients (18.8%) did not. There were no significant differences in the stage of diabetic retinopathy, BCVA, CFT, or MV at baseline between the two groups. Patients in the no insulin group received more steroid injections in the first 12 months of treatment (0.8 vs. 0.2, p = 0.003); however, there …

Artificial intelligence-enabled e-services for justice system services delivery in Namibia
abstract: Background: People living in villages and rural communities across many countries in Africa have limited financial and educational resources to access the services that are provided by the justice system. Thus, making e-services particularly significant. To date, unfortunately, few scholars and researchers have investigated e-services from the justice systems in the context of villages and rural communities in Africa. Objectives: To fill gaps in the literature and address limitations, we conducted this study to empirically investigate how artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to improve and enhance the e-services and deliverables of the justice system in villages and rural communities. Method: The theoretical background for the study is the actor-network theory. The core concepts of the theory, such as translation and immutable mobiles, focus on transformation, processes and events involving actors and actor-networks. The case study approach was applied to the Ministry of Justice (MOJ) and a rural community in Namibia, using the qualitative method. Qualitative data were collected from 18 participants through semi-structured interviews. Results: The findings from the data analysis show that AI can have a positive and significant impact on the justice system e-services and reveal some of the key factors that are fundamentally influencing the process and events. Conclusion: The…

title: Beyond green claims: customer engagement activates green evangelism
abstract: Purpose Credible environmental claims frequently fail to convert into customer advocacy. This study aims to explain why. It positions customer engagement as the mechanism that activates green evangelism from perceived green reputation and perceived green credibility and openness to experience as a trait activated boundary condition on that activation. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 437 patrons of sustainability-positioned culinary establishments across five Indonesian metropolitan areas was analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL 9.30. Engagement was specified as a second-order construct with cognitive, emotional and behavioural facets. Mediation was tested with bias corrected bootstrapping, moderation with multi-group and latent-interaction estimation. Competing models, collinearity and equivalence diagnostics, common method tests and endogeneity checks were run. Findings Reputation and credibility predict evangelism only while engagement is left out of the model. Once engagement is specified, both direct paths fall to non-significance, and engagement remains a strong predictor, the signature of indirect-only mediation. Collinearity is negligible, so redundancy does not account for the pattern. Facet-level decomposition shows the transmission is carried mainly by emotional and behavioural engagement rather than by cognit…

title: Employment protection and firms' reliance on trade credit: international evidence
abstract: Purpose Employment protection legislation (EPL) constitutes a salient institutional source of labor adjustment rigidity, yet firms' financing responses within the supply chain remain underexplored. Drawing on financing advantage theory and operations–finance research on transaction-embedded supplier financing, this paper examines how firms' reliance on trade credit varies with major changes in EPL strictness in a large international sample. It further investigates the operational, financing, and informational mechanisms underlying this association, as well as firm- and country-level boundary conditions that moderate its strength. Design/methodology/approach Based on 315,625 firm-year observations across 29 countries during 1991–2019, this study constructs a reform-based country-year measure of major changes in EPL strictness and estimates fixed-effects panel models. The analysis further examines three mechanisms – operational rigidity, financial constraints, and information asymmetry – and investigates how firm-level characteristics and country-level institutional environments condition the association between EPL reforms and firms' reliance on trade credit. Findings The results suggest that (1) stricter EPL is associated with firms' greater reliance on trade credit; (2) this effect is intensified under greater operational rigidity, tighter financial constraints, and more sever…

title: Application of Lean Six Sigma (LSS) methodology in a small-sized company that sells construction materials: a case study
abstract: Purpose Service duration has a pivotal role in determining both organizational financial performance and customer satisfaction. The purpose of this study is to minimize the variation of the service time in the service procedure to avoid dissatisfaction. Design/methodology/approach The research develops a practical implementation of the Lean Six Sigma methodology, step-by-step, using the DMAIC methodology of define, measure, analyze, improve and control, in reducing the customers' service times. Findings The use of data analysis was important at various phases of the project in order to identify the root causes for the delays in customer service. The result of the method in the customer service process was a significant reduction in the service time by 27.35% and the yield was improved by 15.8%. The estimated annual savings from this project were US$ 80,000, resulting from more customers served per day and increasing returning customers. Practical implications This research may be used in companies that sell construction materials as a tool for managers to increase efficiency and service quality, as well as smaller companies that incorporate service. In addition, the study provided the company with helpful suggestions that will be used in future Lean Six Sigma projects. Thus, practical solutions and guidelines were provided. Originality/value This study addresses a significant g…

title: I nfluencing F actors in A ttracting and R etaining A udiences for H onor of K ings L ive S treaming on D ouyin
abstract: With the development of short-video platforms and game live streaming, Douyin has gradually become an important arena for game content dissemination, audience interaction, and the formation of platform stickiness. As a popular MOBA mobile game, Honor of Kings combines competitive suspense, entertainment value, learning value, and social value in its live-streaming content. Using a narrative literature review approach, this paper examines the question of how Honor of Kings game live streaming on Douyin attracts audiences and increases their continuance watching intention. It reviews existing studies related to Honor of Kings players' motivations, mechanisms of game live streaming, Douyin platform mechanisms, streamer performance, and community operation. The review finds that previous literature has separately revealed the importance of game content value, electronic word-of-mouth, observational learning, uses and gratifications, algorithmic recommendation, gamification mechanisms, technological affordances, user identification, live-streaming humour, and streamer labour. However, these dimensions have rarely been integrated into the specific context of Honor of Kings live streaming on Douyin. This paper argues that audience attraction and retention in Honor of Kings live streaming should be comprehensively understood from three aspects: game content, streamer interaction, and p…

title: Cumulative endpoint and reconstructed 500-m energy-system contributions from individualized pacing-matched trials in 2000-m rowing ergometry
abstract: Objective To evaluate the accuracy with which 500-, 1000-, and 1500-m endpoint trials reproduced each rower’s individualized 2000-m pacing template, estimate cumulative energy-system contributions at 500, 1000, 1500, and 2000 m, and reconstruct contributions across four successive 500-m segments. Methods Twelve trained male provincial-team rowers completed a 2000-m all-out rowing-ergometer reference trial to establish individualized cumulative time, mean power, and mean stroke-rate targets, followed by pacing-matched 500-, 1000-, and 1500-m endpoint trials. Pacing-replication accuracy was evaluated using achieved-minus-target bias, MAE, MAPE, concordance, and Bland–Altman limits of agreement. Energy-system contributions were estimated indirectly using the PCr–La–O 2 framework. Cumulative endpoints and within-rower reconstructed 500-m segments were analyzed separately using repeated-measures analyses with Holm-adjusted comparisons. Results At 500, 1000, and 1500 m, time MAE was 0.050, 0.092, and 1.258 s; power MAE was 0.667, 0.917, and 5.083 W; and stroke-rate MAE was 0.750, 0.396, and 0.359 spm, respectively. Corresponding MAPE values were 0.053–0.431% for time, 0.157–1.339% for power, and 1.239–2.483% for stroke rate. No stable group-level systematic bias was detected after Holm adjustment, although statistical equivalence was not tested. Reconstruction showed a higher estimat…

title: Value Symbiosis Mechanism and Long-Term Development of Humanistic Consumption Space from the Perspective of Scene Theory
abstract: In the process of urban renewal, consumption upgrading promotes humanistic consumption to become the core direction of urban development. However, the transformation of humanistic consumption is facing the challenges of homogenization, lack of cultural core, and insufficient social inclusiveness, which make the consumption space hard to maintain long-term vitality. Taking Beijing 798 Art District as a specific case, this paper adopts scene theory as the analytical framework to examine the transformation logic and internal value symbiosis mechanism of humanistic consumption space. The study found that cultural authenticity is the basis for the symbiosis of cultural value and economic value, over pursue short term business benefits will squeeze the living space of native culture, leading to a scenario core loss and a passenger flow reduction. By balancing short- and long-term development goals, attracting residents to participate in spatial planning, and distributing tourism income rationally, the contradiction of multi-game can be resolved, and the long-term vitality of humanistic consumption space can be maintained. Theoretically, this paper supplements the research on scenario decay and value symbiosis imbalance. Practically, it can provide decision-making reference for renovation of old neighborhoods and industrial heritage cultural and tourism consumption places in domestic …

title: Investigating the effect of diet-induced prediabetes on the HPA-axis, sympathetic nervous system and endogenous opioids in male Sprague-Dawley rats
abstract: Background Prediabetes is associated with metabolic dysfunction that may disrupt neuroendocrine regulation before the onset of overt type 2 diabetes mellitus. Although previous studies have independently examined alterations in the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis, sympathetic nervous system (SNS), and endogenous opioid system during prediabetes, the temporal interactions among these systems during disease progression remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate changes in these interconnected neuroendocrine pathways in a diet-induced prediabetic rats. Methods Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n = 48) were exposed to a standard diet (non-prediabetic, n =24) or an HFHC diet (prediabetic, n =24) for 20 weeks. Prediabetes was confirmed using FBG, OGTT and HbA 1c . Body weight, FBG, and OGTT were measured at weeks 20 to 32, prior to sacrifice. At each point, animals were sacrificed to assess plasma adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), corticosterone, catecholamines (noradrenaline, adrenaline, and dopamine), and β-endorphin using ELISA. Hippocampal GR, MR, β 1 AR, β 2 -AR, MOR, DOR, and KOR mRNA expression were quantified by qRT-PCR. Results At week 20, the PD group exhibited marked reductions in circulating ACTH (30.70 ± 2.10 vs. 42.79 ± 2.91 pg/mL), corticosterone (16.89 ± 0.26 vs. 19.94 ± 0.24 pg/mL), noradrenaline (3.46 ± 0.15 vs. 4.36 ± 0.14 ng/mL), dopamine (1224.…

title: People-to-people food waste management: analyzing discourses on Reddit through the lens of Communities of Practice theory
abstract: Purpose Food waste is a critical global challenge with profound environmental, social, and economic consequences. The growing use of social media and crowdsourced platforms, such as Reddit, provides rich insights into public discourse and collective knowledge construction regarding food waste management. Drawing on Communities of Practice (CoP) Theory, this study analyzes user-generated content on these platforms to examine how digital communities foster shared knowledge and promote sustainable practices for reducing food waste. It specifically explores mutual engagement, shared goals, and proposed solutions within these online spaces. Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative multiple-case study design, this study applies CoP Theory to investigate user-generated content from 22 Reddit communities. The data were thematically analyzed to explore how online interactions support collective knowledge construction, mutual engagement, shared goals, and collaborative problem-solving for food waste reduction. Findings Online communities operate as digital CoPs, where users collaboratively develop strategies to reduce food waste. Key activities include challenging misleading “best before” labels, highlighting inefficiencies in food distribution, and advocating for changes in consumer behavior and corporate policies. Originality/value The study extends CoP Theory to virtual crowdso…

title: Hydro-climatic extremes: trends, anomalies and implications for urban water management
abstract: ABSTRACT Assessing the trends and anomalies of hydro-climatic extremes for improving the urban water managment. Intensifying hydrological and climatic risks are threatening infrastructures and services; therefore, understanding anomalies in hydro-climatic extremes (HCE) is imperative for sustained infrastructure/services. This study investigates the dynamics of HCE and implications for urban water management, with a case of Pokhara Metropolis (Nepal). The city faces recurring challenges from excessive stormwater and streamflow, water scarcity and loss of life. To assess the HCE trends, this study applied Indicators of Hydrologic Alteration (IHA) and ClimPACT2, for both baseline and projected scenarios to streamflow, precipitation and temperature data. The HCE were characterized by coupling indices from the Expert Team on Sector-specific Climate Indices (ET-SCI), IHA parameters and Standardized Anomaly Index (SAI). Results reveal a likely excessive increasing trend in future total annual precipitation (e.g., 0.98–18.32 mm/year at Pokhara Airport) along with severe wet conditions and temperature changes resulting in severe hot SAI, thereby, challenging water supply and public health. Consistent with climatic extremes, extremely wet streamflow is projected to increase (max. monthly flow from 224.00 to 351.10 m3/sec). This study underscores a need for term-based strategies to captu…

title: Hospital pressure and length of stay under organisational reform: evidence from Portuguese public hospitals
abstract: Purpose This study examines how inpatient occupancy pressure and organisational reform are associated with average length of stay (LOS) in Portuguese public hospitals. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses a monthly hospital-level panel dataset for Portuguese public hospitals covering 2015–2025. A dynamic fixed-effects model is estimated to account for persistence in hospital performance, time-invariant hospital heterogeneity and common time shocks. Hospital activity pressure is measured using the reported inpatient occupancy rate, with emergency activity included as an additional demand-side pressure indicator in robustness specifications. Findings The results show strong persistence in hospital length of stay, indicating that organisational patterns are associated with hospital performance over time. Inpatient occupancy pressure is positively associated with length of stay, a pattern consistent with capacity saturation and congestion. The reform indicator is not statistically significant after controlling for persistence, hospital capacity, hospital fixed effects and time effects. Additional interaction models do not provide robust evidence that the occupancy–LOS association differs by reform exposure, hospital size or the post-2024 period. Originality/value The study conceptualises LOS as a dynamic organisational outcome and offers hospital-month evidence from the Po…

title: Developing key ESG performance indicators for sustainable healthcare institutions: a modified Delphi study in South Korea
abstract: Purpose Healthcare institutions are increasingly focusing on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) management, yet systematic performance indicators remain underdeveloped. This study develops and validates ESG performance indicators tailored to healthcare institutions in South Korea using a systematic expert consensus methodology. Design/methodology/approach The process involved two phases. First, 45 preliminary ESG indicators applicable to healthcare institutions were identified through a review of ESG frameworks, healthcare sustainability reports, prior studies, and expert interviews. Second, a two-round modified Delphi survey with healthcare practitioners and academic experts was conducted to assess indicator suitability. Findings A total of 44 ESG performance indicators were established, covering environmental (15 indicators), social (16 indicators), and governance (13 indicators) domains. These indicators reflect the public-interest, non-profit, and patient-centered characteristics of healthcare institutions, thereby addressing the limitations of corporate-centric ESG frameworks. Originality/value This study is among the first to develop and validate ESG performance indicators tailored to healthcare institutions in South Korea. By adapting corporate-centric ESG frameworks to the public-interest, non-profit, and patient-centered characteristics of healthcare, it contr…
venue: Journal of Health Organization and Management

title: An empirical investigation of tourist behavioral intentions for regenerative tourism in Bhaktapur, Nepal
abstract: Purpose Regenerative tourism has gained increasing scholarly attention as it seeks to generate net-positive environmental, cultural and social outcomes. However, empirical research examining tourists’ perceptions and behavioral intentions towards regenerative tourism in tourism destinations remains limited, particularly in culturally rich heritage settings such as Bhaktapur, Nepal. Design/methodology/approach This study addresses the regenerative tourism gap by investigating the psychological and social determinants shaping tourists’ engagement with regenerative tourism in Bhaktapur-Nepal, guided by the extended theory of planned behavior from 230 tourists’ primary survey data. Descriptive statistics and structural equation modeling (SEM) with Smart PLS 4.1 were used to examine the relationships among attitude, curiosity, perceived behavioral control, perceived usefulness, subjective norms and behavioral intention. Findings The findings demonstrate that attitude, curiosity and subjective norms significantly and positively influence Bhaktapur tourists’ intentions to engage in regenerative tourism practices. Perceived usefulness further reinforces behavioral intention, highlighting the importance of perceived environmental, cultural and experiential value creation. Despite these positive orientations, the study reveals a persistent intention–behavior gap among tourists visiting B…

title: The Role of AI in Adopting Green Human Resource Management for a Sustainable Modern Organization: A Systematic Review
abstract: As modern organizations aim for sustainability, integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) practices has become a key strategy. This systematic literature review synthesizes findings from 20 articles published between 2018 and 2024, highlighting the diverse role of AI in promoting sustainability within HRM in contemporary organizations. The review reveals a range of positive impacts of AI on various HRM functions, including recruitment, training, performance evaluation, talent management, and the streamlining of HR processes, all contributing to a competitive advantage for organizations. However, the study also highlights significant concerns raised by employees. These include fears of job loss due to AI-enabled HR functions, reduced importance of human input, privacy issues in data management, and the risk of technological alienation. This synthesis of empirical evidence sheds light on the complex relationship between AI and GHRM, underscoring the need for organizations to address employee concerns while capitalizing on AI to enhance sustainable HRM practices in the modern era.
venue: European Journal of Prosthodontics and Restorative Dentistry

title: Mapping customer journeys in automated restaurants: a process perspective on experience formation
abstract: Purpose Service automation is increasingly redefining service encounters by shifting operational and interactional responsibilities from employees to customers in hospitality operations. This study theorizes how customers experience and make sense of automated services characterized by reduced human support. Drawing on customer-dominant logic, this study aims to examine how value formation unfolds across successive stages. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a multistage qualitative research design, combining in-depth interviews with customers who have experienced automated services and the analysis of user-generated online reviews. Findings Automated services reconfigure service encounters into customer-managed processes in which functional value (e.g., efficiency and reliability) is realized, while emotional value remains fragile. Customers repeatedly adjust expectations, regulate uncertainty, and compensate for the limited human reassurance. These dynamics give rise to detachment as a distinctive, journey-level emotional outcome, rather than a momentary response to isolated service incidents. Originality/value This study conceptualizes automated services as customer-managed, journey-level processes in which value formation unfolds over time and introduces detachment as their distinctive emotional outcome. Extending customer-dominant logic, the findings show how cu…
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Spatial-based Rice Production System Engineering and System Dynamics Modeling for Mitigating Paddy Field Conversion in Tabanan Regency
abstract: Rice field conversion threatens the sustainability of rice production and self-sufficiency in Tabanan Regency, one of Bali Province’s major rice-producing areas. This study aims to determine the rate of rice field conversion, evaluate the balance between rice production and demand, and assess its long-term impacts through dynamic system scenarios. Spatial analysis was conducted using Sentinel-2 imagery processed in Google Earth Engine with Random Forest classification for 2020–2024, followed by dynamic system modeling to simulate rice production and demand from 2020 to 2050. Classification accuracy was very high, with Kappa coefficients ranging from 0.90 to 0.94. Rice field area decreased by an average of 1.71% per year. Under the business-as-usual scenario, rice production is projected to decline gradually and fall below demand around 2038–2039. Model validation produced nRMSE values below 10%, indicating very good model performance. A 50% reduction in land conversion slowed the decline in production, while combining land protection with a 10% increase in rice productivity produced a more stable production trajectory and maintained a surplus through 2050. Therefore, sustainable rice self-sufficiency requires integrated policies that control rice field conversion, protect agricultural land, and improve productivity.

title: Preparation of Duties and Positions for Management at Tasik Madu Jaya Cooperative with Support of Digital and Information Technology
abstract: This study aims to formulate and standardise the distribution of authority, duties, responsibilities, and work procedures within the newly developed organisational structure of Koperasi Tasik Madu Jaya in Malang City. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through structured and semi-structured interviews, directed brainstorming, surveys, and literature reviews involving 22 participants, including cooperative members and representatives of the Malang City Department of Cooperatives, Industry, and Trade. The analysis followed 16 organisational principles: objectivity, specialisation, coordination, authority and responsibility, definition, span of control, balance, continuity, uniformity, unity of command, exception, simplicity, efficiency, scalar principle, flexibility, and equality. The findings led to a standardised distribution of authority, duties, and accountability across governance, management, administrative, financial, legal, digital, and business-unit functions. The organisational structure also gives business units operational autonomy while maintaining accountability to Core Management. In addition, the Information Technology and Digital Division supports member data management, transactions, accounting, inventory, reporting, communication, and digital archiving. The implementation of the organisational fra…

title: Research on the Innovation of Enterprise Economic Management Models in the Digital Economy Era
abstract: With the rapid expansion of the digital economy, enterprises face substantial changes in their operational environment and daily management. Conventional enterprise business management can no longer adapt to the current highly competitive market. This paper looks at how Chinese businesses change their management in the digital age. It describes new features of modern business management, points out three key weaknesses within older management systems, and searches for practical improvement methods. Adopting the literature research method, this study draws on Chinese journal articles, industry survey data, and public cases of enterprise digital transformation. It shows that old-fashioned management ideas, imperfect data systems and a shortage of digitally literate talent are the main barriers to business reform. Companies can address these practical problems by renewing management ideas, building shared data platforms, perfecting talent training and establishing robust data security policies.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Negotiating confidentiality in correctional mental health services: ethical challenges and practice implications in a small island prison system
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore how confidentiality is experienced and negotiated within prison mental healthcare in the Maldives and examine the implications of these experiences for correctional practice, institutional trust and service delivery within a small-island prison system. Design/methodology/approach This study used an exploratory qualitative design and semistructured interviews with 37 participants, including incarcerated individuals (n = 30) and mental health professionals (n = 7) within the Maldives Correctional Service. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings Confidentiality was experienced as a negotiated, context-dependent process shaped by institutional surveillance, custodial responsibilities and social interconnectedness. Four themes emerged: confidentiality under conditions of institutional surveillance; negotiating ethical practice under dual loyalty obligations; social proximity and relational vulnerability in a small-island context; and strengthening ethical confidentiality practices. These dynamics may influence perceptions of privacy, therapeutic willingness and systemic trust. Research limitations/implications Although the findings are drawn from a single correctional system, they offer insights relevant to other socially interconnected correctional settings and highlight the need for clearer confidentiality policies, ethical…

title: BIM-integrated labour productivity measurement: a systematic review
abstract: Purpose Building information modelling (BIM) has the potential to reduce labour intensity in labour productivity (LP) measurement, especially through automated data collection. However, the integration of BIM with LP measurement has not yet been systematically studied. This article aims to examine the knowledge gaps and explore future research directions on BIM-integrated LP measurement through a systematic literature review. Design/methodology/approach Publications retrieved from Scopus and Google Scholar in January 2025 were filtered, with 31 selected for in-depth review and analysed using scientometric and content analysis techniques. Content analysis was guided by a dialectical systems approach covering the concept, methodology and value aspects. Findings The review specifically addresses four research questions aligned with three dimensions of the dialectical systems approach. Based on the status quo of the literature, a framework is proposed that identifies seven knowledge gaps and nine future research directions. Key knowledge gaps include being limited to data collection, the need for manual input and being confined to 3D/4D BIM. Main future directions include exploring BIM for different stages, developing techniques to enhance automation and utilising additional BIM dimensions for LP measurement. Originality/value By employing a dialectical systems approach, this study…

title: Aligning values for engagement: how cultural fit shapes employee advocacy
abstract: Purpose This study examines how specific organizational culture archetypes shape employee advocacy, as measured by the Employee Net Promoter Score (eNPS), through the mediating role of cultural fit. Addressing gaps in existing research, this paper proposes a values-driven approach for diagnosing cultural alignment using the Cultural Fit Assessment Method (CFAM®), which extends the traditional Competing Values Framework by incorporating Digital and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) culture archetypes. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was applied using data collected from 882 employees working in Spanish and Ibero-American firms. The study employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA) to examine the effects of six organizational culture archetypes (People, Innovation, Goals, Norms, Digital, and ESG) on cultural fit and eNPS. Findings The results reveal that Organic Culture Archetypes (People, Goals and Innovation) positively influence cultural fit and thereby enhance employee advocacy. Conversely, Mechanistic Culture Archetypes (Norms, Digital, and ESG) negatively impact cultural fit, potentially diminishing eNPS. Cultural fit was found to fully mediate the relationship between organizational culture and employee advocacy, emphasizing the importance of value alignment in fos…

title: Public Opinion and Audience Perception of Cross-Cultural Sports S tars Endorsements: A Text Mining Study Based on Haaland Endorsement Wang Laoji's Weibo Comment Section
abstract: Under the background of globalization, it is increasingly common for domestic time-honored brands to jointly sign western sports stars to carry out cross-cultural endorsement, but the cultural differences between China and the west can easily lead to polarized audience feedback on social platforms. Most of the existing studies evaluate the marketing effectiveness from the macro perspective of enterprises, and lack the analysis of the discussion content at the social media comment level. Taking the case of Haaland's endorsement of Wanglaoji as an example, this study selected Weibo as the research platform, supported by the theory of source credibility and matching hypothesis, and used two-stage LDA topic modeling based on algorithm modeling and artificial semantics to carry out empirical analysis. The comments were refined into nine sub topics and summarized into three core dimensions: star emotional identity, cross-cultural advertising conflict, and brand international communication. The study found that there was a clear stratification of public opinion, with brand spread to the sea as the mainstream discussion, followed by fan circle evaluation, and cultural adaptation disputes in the minority. This study complements the micro audience demonstration of cross-cultural sports endorsement with strong contrast, and provides reference for domestic time-honored brands to optimize o…

title: Does Green Innovation Alleviate or Aggravate Financing Constraints? — Uncovering a Nonlinear Threshold Effect: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
abstract: Green innovation has been a highly debated topic, which is increasingly important for market entities, especially firms and policy makers. Nevertheless, the advancement of green innovation is constrained by its inherent characteristics: high upfront investment, long payback periods, and substantial risks. This paper selects Chinese A-share listed companies from 2015 to 2024 as the initial research sample, and elaborates on the nonlinear relationship between corporate green innovation (measured by green patent counts) and financing constraints represented by the SA index, filling the research gap in existing relevant studies and providing solid empirical evidence to support the formulation, implementation and optimization of green innovation supporting policies. Using panel data, fixed-effects models, and heterogeneity tests, this study examines the inverted U-shaped relationship between green innovation and financing constraints. The findings offer empirical clarification on how green innovation alleviates financing constraints, and carry meaningful implications for stimulating market vitality and advancing high-quality green transformation.

title: Housing price prediction in Ireland: a machine learning framework integrating geospatial encodings and macroeconomic indicators
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop and evaluate a machine learning framework for predicting residential property prices in Ireland using the complete Irish Property Price Register, a population-complete data set of 736,002 arm’s-length transactions spanning January 2010 to March 2026. It formally quantifies the marginal contribution of geospatial, structural and macroeconomic data modalities. Design/methodology/approach A multi-modal predictive framework integrates structural transaction data, address-derived geospatial location signals via Bayesian out-of-fold target encoding and macroeconomic indicators from the Central Statistics Office. Five models are trained and evaluated, including Ridge Regression, Random Forest and three HistGradientBoosting variants on an 80/20 train-test split. Findings Geospatial location features increase R² by 0.2552, from 0.3494 to 0.6046, reducing mean absolute error by €28,271 per property. Macroeconomic lag features covering the consumer price index, unemployment and earnings change R² by less than 0.0001. The best model, HistGradientBoosting v3, achieves R² = 0.6046 and MAE = €80,755 on 144,470 held-out observations. Research limitations/implications The study is constrained by the absence of floor area, bedroom count and BER information for most transactions in the Irish Property Price Register. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ …

title: Job Order Costing for Production Cost and Selling Price Decisions at Chariyah Catering
abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes the application of Job Order Costing in determining the cost of goods manufactured (COGM) at Chariyah Catering and evaluates the implications of the resulting cost information for selling price decisions. Research Method: A descriptive quantitative case-study design was applied using primary data obtained through observation, interviews, and documentation. Three customer orders were analyzed by identifying direct material, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead costs, calculating order-specific COGM, and comparing the results with the business's existing costing method. Results and Discussion: Job Order Costing produced COGM of Rp29,405,000, Rp42,721,000, and Rp58,928,500 for the three orders, respectively, exceeding the business-method estimates of Rp17,500,000, Rp27,000,000, and Rp34,500,000. The differences mainly reflect broader recognition of manufacturing overhead. A 10% cost-plus pricing simulation also generated higher prices than those currently applied. Implications: Some overhead items relied on estimated resource utilization, only three orders were analyzed, and market acceptance was not tested. The findings support systematic order-level cost recording and clearer overhead-allocation bases for pricing decisions. title: TMPE: online power time-series forecasting via truncated Monte Carlo and prior experience replay
Machine learning for low-carbon concrete strength prediction: methods and trends
abstract: Low-carbon concrete (LCC) is an effective approach to reduce carbon dioxide emissions in construction while maintaining adequate compressive strength (CS). Machine learning (ML) methods have been increasingly applied to predict the CS of LCC; however, existing studies remain fragmented in terms of data sources, material systems, modelling strategies, and evaluation criteria. This review provides a systematic synthesis of 172 peer-reviewed studies on ML-based CS prediction of LCC. Bibliometric analysis is conducted to evaluate the representativeness of the literature database, followed by an examination of research evolution across methodological and material dimensions. Mainstream ML approaches are analysed with respect to modelling mechanisms, feature engineering, and performance evaluation, and qualitatively compared using a unified five-point scoring framework. The results reveal a clear shift from single-model approaches towards ensemble learning, Bayesian optimisation, and multi-objective modelling, particularly for systems incorporating supplementary cementitious materials and recycled constituents. Key challenges and future research directions are discussed, including interpretable ML, climate-adaptive modelling, and emerging artificial intelligence-assisted design frameworks, to support more robust and generalisable ML applications in LCC design.

Enhancing Basketball Result Prediction Performance Through Innovative Feature Engineering
abstract: Sports result prediction is a long-standing topic. Yet most existing studies rely heavily on team-scale data and overlook individual players, leaving abstract qualities like chemistry unexplored. This study emphasizes feature engineering to holistically capture each team's power, style, pace, and chemistry. Since conventional stats are insufficient for modern basketball, novel features are constructed manually based on NBA metrics and in-depth knowledge of the game—including TS%, DNP quantification, weighted standard deviation, winning streaks, and starter-bench depth—via an aggregation step, and game-lag was applied to prevent data leakage. This rich feature engineering successfully integrated players' differentiated performances into machine learning, enabling the model to capture the team's true level in a nuanced way. XGBoost, Random Forest, and CART were selected as the prediction model. The results revealed that these new features significantly boost prediction accuracy. The analysis of feature importance also underscores the significant role these features play.

Early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke: an explainable model based on routine clinical data
abstract: Background Accurate early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke is essential for prognostic communication, early management planning, and resource allocation. However, clinically applicable and interpretable prediction tools based on routinely collected data remain limited. Methods In this single-center retrospective prediction-model study, we analyzed 770 adults with acute ischemic stroke admitted within 24 h of symptom onset. Baseline clinical and early laboratory variables were collected. After an 80/20 train–test split, key predictors were selected using cross-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) in the training set. Several supervised learning models were developed and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated. The final gradient boosting machine (GBM) model was interpreted using TreeSHAP, and an online Shiny-based calculator was developed. Results LASSO identified 12 predictors. Test-set discrimination was similar across models, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.854 to 0.867. The final GBM achieved AUCs of 0.910 in the training set and 0.872 in the test set, with corresponding areas under the precision–recall curve of 0.814 and 0.741. Calibration was satisfactory in both sets. SHAP analyses identified NIHSS, age, and C-re…

title: A Multi-Scale Traffic-State Gated Attention Network for Bus Arrival Time Prediction
abstract: Accurate bus arrival time prediction supports passenger information services and transit dispatching, but irregular sampling and time-varying traffic conditions make the task strongly nonlinear. This paper proposes a Spatial Attention Multi-Scale Traffic-State Gated Long Short-Term Memory (SA-MS-TG-LSTM) network. Seven trajectory features are constructed from Global Positioning System (GPS) records, including acceleration, congestion index, and speed volatility. Scale-preserving Spatial Feature Attention (SFA) first reweights the feature dimensions, and three Traffic-State Gated Long Short-Term Memory (TG-LSTM) branches subsequently encode the latest 5, 10, and 15 time steps. Their outputs are concatenated and mapped to the remaining travel time. Experiments are conducted on 8,834 GPS records from 293 trips on a single bus route (Route 86). Under a controlled setting in which all recurrent models use a hidden size of 16, one recurrent layer, and at most 50 training epochs, SA-MS-TG-LSTM achieves the best aggregate performance, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.056 min, mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.762 min, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 12.06%, and coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of 0.9631. Compared with the Convolutional Neural Network--Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN-GRU), it reduces RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by 6.30%, 5.57%, and 11.26%, respectively. Trip-level …

title: From bias to bots: discrimination and AI service preference
abstract: Purpose While artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled services have become increasingly prevalent, little is known about how discriminatory service encounters influence consumers’ preference for AI-based service providers. This research aims to investigate whether – and why – perceived discrimination in human service encounters increases consumers’ preference for AI-driven service options. Design/methodology/approach Three studies were conducted to test the proposed framework. Study 1 used an autobiographical recall design, Study 2a experimentally manipulated discrimination, and Study 2b used a 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design. Mediation and moderated mediation effects were examined using PROCESS. Findings Across the three studies, perceived discrimination was associated with greater preference for AI service providers through reduced social comfort with human providers and enhanced perceptions of AI ethicality. Cultural tightness consistently strengthened the social-comfort pathway, whereas its moderating influence on perceived AI ethicality and the direct effect was less consistent. Practical implications The findings offer actionable insights for designing inclusive service systems, deploying ethical AI solutions and enhancing customer experience strategies. A sensemaking perspective on the drivers, boundary conditions, and outcomes of frontline employee bricolage
abstract: Purpose Frontline employees (FLEs) often face significant challenges as they strive to achieve high levels of job performance despite having limited resources. However, research exploring the determinants, boundary conditions, and outcomes of FLE bricolage remains limited. Grounded in sensemaking theory, our study proposes that FLE digital integration enhances their bricolage, which, in turn, enhances adaptive selling and job performance. The relationship between digital integration and bricolage is proposed to be positively moderated by manager intellectual stimulation. Design/methodology/approach We used a mixed methods design to assess the robustness of our proposed framework through (1) an analysis of survey responses from 115 business-to-business (B2B) FLEs (Study 1), (2) a qualitative exploration with 12 B2B FLEs (Study 2), and (3) an experimental study (Study 3) with 210 FLEs. Findings In line with our proposed framework, FLE digital integration enhances FLE bricolage, and this relationship is moderated by manager intellectual stimulation. Furthermore, FLE bricolage increases adaptive selling and job performance. Practical implications Organizations should invest in promoting the adoption of digital technologies among FLEs to enhance employee bricolage. Organizations should also train their managers to display intellectually stimulating behaviors to enhance the effects o…

title: Circular design strategies in the post-consumption journey: a systematic literature review of service design for circular fashion SMEs
abstract: Purpose Post-consumption processes are increasingly acknowledged as a critical component of facilitating circular fashion systems within small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Nonetheless, research in this area often remains fragmented and dispersed across disciplinary domains. There is a limited understanding of how service design supports sustainable consumption and what challenges consumers encounter throughout the post-consumption journey. This study aims to systematically map and synthesise the fragmented research concerning post-consumption processes by critically analysing key service touchpoints, consumer pain points and service design strategies to develop an integrated framework for circular fashion SMEs. Design/methodology/approach This study systematically reviews 96 peer-reviewed articles selected from an initial pool of 997 publications using PRISMA guidelines. The data are analysed through inductive thematic analysis supported by NVivo to identify recurring post-consumption stages, consumer interactions and challenges and literature-discussed service design strategies. This is complemented by bibliometric analysis using CiteSpace. Findings Post-consumption functions as an interconnected, multi-stage service journey shaped by recurring touchpoints, consumer pain points and strategic interventions across usage, evaluation, after-sales service and disposal. title: Characteristics of Public Service Innovation in the SAYANG GADIS Program at the Department of Population and Civil Registration of Kediri Regency
abstract: Population administration services are essential to citizens’ access to legal identity, yet requirements to visit service points can exclude people with limited mobility. The Population and Civil Registration Office of Kediri Regency introduced SAYANG GADIS (Sahaja Datang Bahagia Disabilitas) to provide home visits and door-to-door services. This study examines the program through Rogers’ five innovation attributes: relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability, and observability. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation involving the Head of Population Registration Services, program staff, and service recipients or their families. Analysis followed Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña’s stages of data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that the program improves access for residents unable to visit service points and has adapted its target groups to needs identified during implementation. Challenges include recipients’ conditions, internet connectivity, access to locations, and hospital procedures. Practice-based adjustments indicate some trialability, although no formal training or documented trial process was identified. Improved access to electronic identity card recording and issuance, together with positive recipient responses, makes the pro…

title: Penguatan Budaya Meneliti melalui Pelatihan Karya Tulis Ilmiah Berbasis Riset bagi Siswa dan Guru SMA Kristen Yahya Bandung
abstract: Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan budaya meneliti di lingkungan sekolah menengah melalui pelatihan penulisan karya tulis ilmiah berbasis riset bagi guru dan siswa SMA Kristen Yahya Bandung. Budaya meneliti merupakan bagian penting dari implementasi Kurikulum Merdeka karena mendorong pembelajaran berpusat pada siswa dan memperkuat keterampilan berpikir kritis serta literasi ilmiah. Pelatihan penulisan karya tulis ilmiah ini dilaksanakan dalam dua sesi, yaitu untuk siswa dan guru, dengan metode ceramah, diskusi interaktif, serta eksplorasi mini. Kegiatan diikuti oleh 120 siswa dan 20 guru, dan difokuskan pada pengenalan langkah-langkah penelitian sederhana yang relevan dengan 17 Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan (Sustainable Development Goals/ SDGs). Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan peningkatan partisipasi dan pemahaman peserta terhadap konsep dasar penelitian. Siswa mampu menyusun kerangka karya tulis ilmiah sederhana, merumuskan topik penelitian kontekstual, serta menunjukkan kesadaran ilmiah yang lebih baik. Guru memperoleh wawasan baru mengenai strategi pembimbingan penelitian dan variasi model penelitian yang sesuai untuk tingkat sekolah menengah. Kegiatan ini berkontribusi terhadap penguatan profil pelajar Pancasila, pengembangan budaya akademik, serta peningkatan literasi ilmiah di lingkungan sekolah. title: The impact of AI chatbot service quality on consumer purchase intention: the cognitive and affective mediating mechanisms
abstract: Introduction The increasing prevalence of artificial intelligence chatbots in e-commerce raises questions about how the service quality dimensions of AI chatbots may influence consumer purchase intentions. Drawing on Expectation-Confirmation Theory, the Information Systems Success Model, and the Technology Acceptance Model, this study proposes a conceptual framework to examine these relationships. Methods Survey data were collected from 493 Chinese consumers with prior experience using AI chatbots. The study examined perceived personalization, social presence, information quality, and human-AI service continuity as possible antecedents of purchase intention. Perceived usefulness and satisfaction were treated as mediating variables. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used for the analysis with 5,000 bootstrapped resamples. Results Perceived personalization, social presence, information quality, and human-AI service continuity were associated with perceived usefulness. Additionally, perceived personalization, information quality, and human-AI service continuity were positively associated with satisfaction. Conversely, social presence did not show a significant direct effect on satisfaction.
