title: A single-field model of cosmic expansion with a geometric disformal coupling
abstract: We propose a mechanism that unifies the cosmic expansion history using a single scalar field coupled to a disformal lapse function. In the Jordan frame, where matter is minimally coupled, the lapse modifies the Hubble rate measured by matter observers. As a result, matter observers perceive three successive expansion epochs, including early inflation, intermediate deceleration, and late time acceleration, even though the underlying Einstein-frame dynamics exhibits no distinct phases. The lapse function is constrained to satisfy the horizon entropy condition and to approach unity asymptotically, ensuring agreement with standard Einstein-frame dynamics at late times. In this framework, a small early-time value of the lapse compresses the physical time experienced by matter observers, producing the appearance of a rapid inflationary expansion occurring within a very short interval of their proper time. The time dilation effect induced by the lapse is alleviated at late times as the lapse approaches unity. A Noether symmetry approach is implemented to derive the scalar potential, which is exponential and leads to smooth power-law evolution in the Einstein frame. Although such solutions are known to have phenomenological limitations, the disformal lapse modifies the effective expansion dynamics experienced by matter observers while preserving the simplicity of power-law evolution.

title: Pion-photon Transition Form Factor with Analytic Coupling
abstract: We investigate the pion-photon transition form factor within the framework of analytic QCD. A comparison is performed between experimental data and perturbative QCD based on conventional and analytic versions of perturbation theory with the “massive” form of the twist-four contribution. We show that conventional perturbation theory fails to reproduce the data, while the analytic version demonstrates good agreement with experiment.

title: Energy value of cereal grains for broiler chickens. I. Variation within and among grain species, and effect of exogenous enzymes
abstract: Context Cereal grains are the major source of energy for broiler chickens. Energy available to chickens varies widely within and among cereal species and must be measured to develop near-infrared (NIR) calibrations for predicting values when formulating diets. Aims To measure apparent metabolisable energy (AME) content of cereal grains sourced from a wide range of species, cultivars, growing conditions and regions, including outside Australia. Methods Cereal grains (wheat 136, barley 63, oats 3, triticale 42, sorghum 66, maize 11, rice 2) were selected with a range of chemical and physical characteristics from normal harvest, frosted, sprouted, screened (< >2–2.2 mm) and irrigated samples. Twenty-six experiments were linked, statistically, into one experiment, by incorporating in each experiment at least 30% of grains used previously. Single sex groups of five birds per cage reared under a controlled environment were fed ad libitum diets containing 80% grain from Day 22 to Day 28 of age. Feed intake was measured over 7 days and grain AME over the final 4 days. Diets in 10 experiments were fed with and without exogenous xylanase and phytase enzymes. Key results The mean and range in grain AME (MJ/kg as fed) were as follows: wheat 12.62, 2.81; barley 11.41, 3.08; triticale 12.93, 3.82; sorghum 14.50, 1.60; maize 15.37, 0.59; oats 11.85, 1.90; rice 15.93, 0.35. AME intake (M…

title: Navigating the systemic labyrinth: the dual-track breakthrough of student-athletes under China's “Integration of Sports and Education”
abstract: Introduction Although dual career (DC) development has received growing international attention, the psychosocial experiences of high-level student-athletes (HLSAs) within China's evolving Integration of Sports and Education (ISE) context remain underexplored. Methods This study adopted an interpretivist qualitative design and used Reflexive Thematic Analysis to examine retrospective developmental accounts from 19 Chinese HLSAs admitted to university through the high-level sports team pathway. Results Athletic achievement expanded access to higher education but did not automatically secure stable competence, legitimacy, or belonging across academic and athletic settings. Effort often remained within HLSAs' control even when its returns became uncertain because of injury, bodily limits, competitive conditions, and fluctuating performance, requiring athletes to recalibrate causal expectations and perceptions of what could still be changed. Institutional support, recognition, and opportunities also varied with athletic standing, making the quality of integration psychologically consequential beyond the formal coexistence of sport and education. Discussion These findings conceptualize DC as a process of conditional inclusion. Chinese HLSAs navigate a systemically structured but psychologically experienced labyrinth, in which breakthrough occurs when athletic achievement is transfor…

title: Molecular Insights into the Inhibition Mechanisms of Modified PVCap Kinetic Inhibitors in Hydrogen Sulfide-Containing Gas Hydrate Systems
abstract: Abstract Gas hydrate blockage threatens pipeline safety in sour gas reservoirs, where hydrogen sulfide (H2S) accelerates hydrate formation and the conventional kinetic inhibitor poly N-vinylcaprolactam (PVCap) severely degrades. Microsecond-level molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and quantum chemical calculations were performed to investigate hydrate nucleation and growth in a 30% H2S environment using unmodified PVCap and three functionalized copolymers: PVCap-co-Apy, PVCap-co-Pip, and PVCap-co-n-butyl. Based on cage type distributions, molecular diffusion, and interaction energies, the inhibitory efficacy follows PVCap-co-Apy > PVCap-co-n-butyl > PVCap-co-Pip > PVCap. The inhibitors barely delay initial nucleation but significantly suppress postnucleation rapid growth. PVCap-co-Apy shows the best performance and a pronounced selective inhibition of 51262 cages, driven by its highly hydrophilic N-acryloylpyrrolidine group that preferentially hydrogen-bonds with water and disrupts local hydrogen-bonded networks. PVCap-co-n-butyl regulates kinetics via a hydrophobic mechanism: the n-butyl group forms local hydrophobic domains that preferentially accumulate methane rather than H2S, modifying the local guest composition and weakening the driving force for cage formation, though steric hindrance partially shields adjacent polar groups. PVCap-co-Pip shows limited efficacy…

title: Oleer: optimized layer-based and energy-efficient routing protocol with enabled Q-learning for underwater sensor networks
Rethinking Powerline Energy Harvesting: From Induced Voltage to Usable Power
abstract: Powerline magnetic energy harvesting offers a non-invasive route to supply low-power monitoring nodes, but a substantial induced voltage does not necessarily imply that usable electrical power can be delivered through the power-conversion interface. This paper investigates that voltage-to-power gap using a ferrite-core inductive harvester. The front end was designed for an induced voltage of approximately 6 V and produced 5.33 V AC under a controlled 10 A, 50 Hz line condition. Despite this measured voltage, the bridge-rectifier output was 0 V DC, preventing the real harvesting chain from establishing usable downstream energy. A simplified source-impedance simulation qualitatively reproduces the progression from stable rectification for an ideal source to severe voltage collapse when source impedance and load are introduced. The results support a system-level interpretation in which source impedance, rectification loss, and interface loading jointly constrain energy delivery. Powerline harvesters should therefore be evaluated around loaded power delivery rather than induced voltage alone.

title: Simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (STAR-RIS) with hybrid wind and vibration energy harvesting
“We Belong, But Not Fully”: Recognition, Racialisation, and School Belonging Among Immigrant-Background Students in Spain
abstract: Abstract Questions of recognition and belonging are central to modern migration and integration debates, yet the everyday school experiences of racialized immigrant-background youth remain underexplored, particularly in Southern Europe. This qualitative study examines how these students negotiate recognition, exclusion, and belonging in Spanish secondary schools. Grounded in Critical Race Theory, the research employed in-depth interviews alongside an adapted photovoice approach, utilizing photo-elicitation to capture the daily realities and perspectives of 28 participants. The findings revealed that school belonging is not just a byproduct of formal inclusion policies. Instead, it is a daily struggle shaped by moments of acceptance and rejection within a color-evasive institution. Students described everyday interactions tied to language, race, and nationality that welcomed them into the school community while simultaneously questioning their competence, voice, and right to be there. Ultimately, recognition functions as a conditional, unevenly distributed resource. However, rather than being passive subjects, these students showed a sharp awareness of these dynamics. They actively used bicultural competence, resistant capital, and identity work to challenge exclusionary boundaries. By centering youth voices, this study shows how belonging emerges from the tension between instit…
venue: Journal of International Migration and Integration

title: Costs and parameters of BEV electrification: a comprehensive review of battery system innovations, vehicle-level integration, and energy system synergies
abstract: Abstract Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) are crucial for decarbonizing transportation, with their market penetration depending on cost structures and innovative technologies. This review analyzes key cost and performance parameters along the vertical integration axis of BEV electrification, from battery cells to energy system integration. It highlights innovative battery technologies, advanced pack integration, vehicle cost structures, and energy system synergies, offering researchers and manufacturers guidance for technology selection and holistic system integration.

title: Corrosion-induced surface reconstruction enhances RuO 2 /NiFe(OH) x for efficient hydrogen evolution reaction
abstract: NiFe hydroxide has emerged as a highly promising electrocatalyst in water electrolysis, yet its application in catalyzing the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) remains challenging. Herein, we report a corrosion-reconstruction strategy to fabricate RuO2 nanocluster-endowed NiFe hydroxide [RuO2/NiFe(OH)x ] as an efficient electrocatalyst for HER application. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provide insight into the HER mechanism, revealing that the reconstructed surface enriched with RuO2 nanoclusters optimally adsorbs water molecules. This modification also induces a shift of the *H adsorption site from oxygen atoms to ruthenium atoms due to electron transfer effects, facilitating the desorption of *H and promoting efficient H2 formation. The synthesized RuO2/NiFe(OH)x catalyst delivers prominent HER activity (149 mV at 100 mA cm-2) and robust operational stability in a water-splitting device, sustaining 200 mA cm-2 for 100 h with almost no obvious voltage increment. Importantly, the fabrication of a large-area electrode demonstrates that this simple, room-temperature corrosion-reconstruction strategy is a promising and viable route for the application of HER electrocatalysts.

title: Energy value of cereal grains for broiler chickens. III. Suitability of NIR for predicting AME of wheat for diet formulation
abstract: Context Cereal grains vary widely in energy content, which can result in poor performance of chickens when wrongly assumed apparent metabolisable energy (AME) values are used in diet formulation. Aims To evaluate the suitability of using near-infrared spectrometry (NIR) calibrations to predict AME content of grains when formulating diets for chickens. Methods Measured AME contents for 111 cereal grains were used to determine the accuracy of their prediction by (i) calculations based on physiochemical measurements, (ii) near-infrared spectrometry (NIR) calibration, and (iii) two published values for each grain type. Suitability of using NIR calibrations to predict AME content of wheat was evaluated in a chicken growth experiment. Wheat with NIR-predicted AME content of 13.59 MJ/kg as fed was formulated into four diets from starter to withdrawal or substituted by another wheat with NIR-predicted AME content of 12.45 MJ/kg as fed. Key results The NIR calibration was the most accurate method for predicting grain AME content for broiler chickens of the 111 grains from different grain species. Chickens fed the NIR-predicted higher-AME wheat diet had a lower feed conversion ratio (FCR g feed/g gain), resulting from non-significant faster growth rate and lower feed intake, than chickens fed the diet based on wheat with a predicted lower AME content when measured over a 42-day period. C…

title: Stochastic multi-objective optimization for office energy saving with occupant uncertainty
abstract: Purpose To address the insufficient consideration of occupant behavior uncertainty in multi-objective optimization for office building energy efficiency by proposing a stochastic optimization framework that incorporates multiple occupant behaviors into the optimization process. Design/methodology/approach Field data from typical office buildings in Ningbo were used to develop four occupant behavior models (occupancy, air conditioning, shading and window operation). These models were integrated into EnergyPlus simulations within a stochastic multi-objective optimization framework based on NSGA-II and sample average approximation (SAA). Findings The proposed framework improved the robustness of the optimization results under occupant behavior uncertainty. The balanced solution reduced fluctuation ranges compared to the original model, achieving significant energy savings while revealing a trade-off with thermal comfort. Among the investigated design alternatives, a window-to-wall ratio of 0.25 provided the best overall performance. Originality/value This study presents a practical stochastic multi-objective optimization framework that integrates empirically derived occupant behavior models with SAA and NSGA-II. By embedding occupant behavior uncertainty directly into the optimization process rather than relying on post-hoc robustness analysis, the proposed framework provides a mo…

title: From cost to efficiency: photovoltaic modules allocation to maximizing energy production while minimizing costs with building information modeling
abstract: Purpose This article aims to develop an automated building information modeling (BIM)-based process to optimize the allocation of photovoltaic (PV) modules on building roofs. The goal is to maximize energy production while minimizing implementation costs, advancing digitalization in sustainable project planning within the Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operations (AECO) sector. Design/methodology/approach The research integrates visual programming in Dynamo with Python scripts to simulate and compare combinations of 21 PV module models from four brands. The model extracts geometric information directly from a Revit BIM model, calculates energy production and costs for each configuration, and automatically allocates the most efficient arrangement. The approach is demonstrated through two experiments and compared against a real PV system installed at the Federal University of Pernambuco (UFPE). Findings The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm identifies the most efficient cost–production configuration of PV modules. Experiment 1 achieved the highest daily production (2,723.63 kWh/day) at a total cost of USD $387,575.45, while Experiment 2 achieved a better cost–benefit balance (2,630.09 kWh/day at USD $370,504.08). Compared to the current UFPE layout, the optimized configurations increased energy production. The study confirms that integrating BIM with al…

title: Polymer-Based Hydrogels for Chemical Biosensing: From Bioreceptor Integration to Smart Applications
abstract: Abstract In recent years, flexible, wearable, and implantable chemical sensors and biosensors have become crucial in biomedical engineering. These flexible devices enable the noninvasive, real-time monitoring of biochemical markers in biofluids, from blood to the most accessible ones that enable noninvasive monitoring (sweat, tears, saliva, and interstitial fluid) as indicators of the health status. In their development, polymer-based hydrogels have emerged as the material of choice and have recently started to attract increasing attention due to advantages in terms of biocompatibility, surface area, and chemical tunability. Here, we provide an overview of the structural polymers according to their nature (natural vs synthetic), giving a special focus on the use of conductive polymers. Then, we discuss the strategies to integrate the bioreceptor to provide the hydrogels with the necessary selectivity toward biomarker detection. Finally, we go through emerging trends where hydrogels are employed in smart formats beyond the simple performance of the detection. As an overall, the integration of polymer-based hydrogels with advanced bioreceptor strategies and smart functionalities is driving the development of next-generation wearable and implantable biosensors, paving the way for noninvasive, continuous, and personalized diagnostics.

title: Bridging sustainability and accountability: the role of ESG integration in corporate governance
abstract: Purpose Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations are increasingly shaping corporate decision-making, influencing financial performance and stakeholder trust. This study examines how Ugandan firms integrate ESG principles into governance structures to enhance sustainability and long-term value creation. Using corporate governance theories and empirical data from multinational firms operating in Uganda, the study explores ESG's role in risk management, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder engagement. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was employed, utilizing semi-structured interviews with 15 board members, sustainability officers, and governance experts. Document analysis of sustainability reports, corporate governance codes, and ESG policies further informs the study. Thematic analysis identifies key patterns in ESG implementation. Findings Findings revealed that regulatory compliance, stakeholder expectations, and long-term value creation drive ESG integration. Firms with strong ESG frameworks benefit from enhanced reputation and investor confidence. However, greenwashing, inconsistent reporting standards, and resistance from traditional governance structures hinder implementation. Practical implications While regulatory influence is significant, jurisdictional inconsistencies create compliance challenges. Companies embedding ESG at the boar…

title: Enterprise Integration Architecture using Event Mesh: A Reference Framework for Cloud-Native and AI-Ready Enterprises
abstract: Modern enterprises integrate heterogeneous on-premises, multi-cloud, SaaS, IoT, and AI-enabled systems, creating coordination, scalability, resilience, governance, and real-time context challenges for conventional integration approaches. Although Event-Driven Architecture and event streaming are established, the literature provides limited vendor-neutral guidance that integrates Event Mesh federation, event governance, observability, hybrid-cloud deployment, and selected agentic-AI integration concerns into one enterprise reference framework. This study proposes the Enterprise Event Mesh Reference Architecture (EEMRA) to address that gap. Using Design Science Research Methodology, the study identifies the integration problem, synthesizes prior literature, develops the EEMRA artifact, performs a qualitative capability comparison, and examines illustrative enterprise cases. The framework organizes enterprise systems, event enablement and production, the Event Mesh fabric, integration services, event consumers, and cross-cutting governance and observability. Principal contributions include EEMRA, a six-responsibility architecture model, the Enterprise Event Taxonomy Framework, an Agentic Integration Architecture, an Event Mesh + Model Context Protocol integration pattern, and the Enterprise Nervous System Principle. Findings indicate that Event Mesh can provide a useful asynchrono…

title: Intelligent self-evolving design method of a high-load-bearing hydrostatic oil groove
abstract: Abstract Hydrostatic oil grooves in friction pairs are responsible for guiding, storing, and distributing lubricating oil and are widely applied to ultrahigh-power hydraulic motors of tunnel boring machines, aerospace variable pumps, and hydrostatic precision guideways/spindles of high-end industrial mother machines. The traditional design methods for oil groove patterns highly rely on the designer’s experience and size optimization of preset shapes, making it difficult to achieve optimal lubrication. Therefore, this study proposes the intelligent self-evolving design method of oil grooves, in which the AI-assisted generalized pattern search algorithm (GPS+AI) is designed to make an oil groove pattern self-evolve toward maximizing the load-bearing capacity according to the friction pair’s contact force feedback from a lubrication model. The designed oil groove pattern is machined onto the piston of a hydraulic motor and is experimentally evaluated for its lubrication load-bearing capacity through a homemade quasiactual roller–piston pair testing rig. Comparing two traditional oil grooves, the new oil groove can reduce the friction torque (contact force) by a maximum of 88%, which is very significant for improving the efficiency and lifespan of ultrahigh power hydraulic motors (power > 106 W), especially under the dual-carbon target.

title: Extension Design for the Application of Balakka Leaf Botanical Pesticide to Control Aphids on Red Chili Plants in Padang Bolak District
abstract: Red chili cultivation in Padang Bujur Village, Padang Bolak District, faces aphid (Aphis gossypii) infestation and heavy reliance on synthetic pesticides. Locally abundant balakka leaves (Phyllanthus emblica L.) offer a potential botanical pesticide for agricultural extension. This study designed an extension activity, characterized the target farmers, and assessed acceptance and adoption of the proposed innovation. A descriptive quantitative study was conducted from April to May 2026 using interviews and closed questionnaires with 30 red chili farmers; questionnaire responses were analyzed using a Likert scale. The extension components received an acceptance score of 86.18%, classified as highly appropriate. Following the activity, 12 farmers (40.00%) adopted the balakka-leaf botanical pesticide, exceeding the target of 10 farmers (33.33%). These findings support the feasibility of the extension design and illustrate the potential to integrate locally available botanical resources into environmentally friendly pest-management extension.

title: A toolpath-driven design method for continuous fibre-reinforced polymer additive manufacturing of lattice structures
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to develop a toolpath-driven parametric design methodology for additively manufactured continuous carbon fibre-reinforced lattice structures to overcome design difficulties from fibre deposition constraints, enable reinforcement of cellular architectures, and incorporate manufacturing limitations and fibre-orientation control. Design/methodology/approach An integrated workflow combines evolutionary computation and parametric mapping to optimise four key variables – unit cell size, infill size, deposition direction and material ratio. The workflow also guides reinforcement using a shortest-path algorithm that directly generates continuous, printer-ready toolpaths bypassing conventional slicing steps. The framework was implemented using in-house computational tools and validated by fabricating hexagonal lattice specimens printed with continuous carbon fibre; results were compared to parts produced using commercial slicers for mechanical performance and surface finish. Findings The toolpath-driven approach preserves fibre continuity and enables explicit orientation control while embedding manufacturing constraints into the design loop. Fabricated hexagonal lattice specimens printed with the proposed method exhibited improved stiffness and better surface finish than equivalent parts produced with conventional slicers. The framework streamlines t…

title: Angle–torque relationship and muscular activity patterns during concentric contractions with a novel variable cam system
abstract: Introduction Understanding the angle -torque relationship requires recognizing that torque can differ across contraction modes. This study aimed to analyze the performance of the Variable Moment Arm Cam® (VMAC®) by examining torque production and muscle activation during concentric leg extension contractions across the full range of motion (ROM) (100°–0°) and comparing them with those obtained using an isokinetic dynamometer. Methods In total, 22 young men (20.55 ± 2.19 years; 175.41 ± 7.21 cm; 72.80 ± 9.90 kg; 18.00 ± 5.83% body fat; 23.63 ± 2.82 kg·m⁻ 2 ) participated in four randomized moments of torque and muscle activity assessments, two using the VMAC® and two using an isokinetic dynamometer. Torque and muscle activity data were synchronized and recorded across the entire ROM (100°–0°) and evaluated at 5° intervals. Results The VMAC® system produced strength curves that closely matched those observed when using the isokinetic dynamometer across the initial and mid-ROM joint angles (100°–35°), peaking around mid-ROM (70°–65°). Muscle activity differed across conditions while the torque production remained similar. Conclusion The VMAC® generated torque patterns comparable to isokinetic dynamometry, showing the strongest alignment at mid-ROM, supporting the use of this system to replicate natural human strength curves while highlighting the opportunity to refine cam geometry…
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: Drivers of artificial intelligence adoption for construction risk management: a developing country perspective
abstract: Purpose Despite the growing potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance construction risk management through predictive analytics, automation, and data-driven decision-making, its adoption within developing-country construction industries remains limited and poorly understood. This study aims to examine the key drivers influencing the adoption of AI technologies for construction risk management within the Ghanaian construction industry. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey approach was adopted, underpinned by the technology–organisation–environment framework. Data were gathered from 94 construction professionals in Ghana using a structured questionnaire. Mean score ranking, one-sample t-test, and exploratory factor analysis using principal component analysis with varimax rotation were used for data analysis. Findings The findings reveal that sustainability reporting pressures, availability of quality data, competitive advantage, cross-functional data integration, and policy focus on climate and resilience are the most influential drivers of AI adoption in construction risk management. The factor analysis further grouped the drivers into four interrelated dimensions: strategic and sustainability-oriented ecosystem enablers; organisational digital maturity and technical capability; market, compliance, and performance-driven enablers; and foundational leaders…
venue: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology

title: Surface-Functionalized Niosomes for Targeted Drug Delivery: Design Strategies, Molecular Mechanisms and Clinical Translation
abstract: Surface-functionalized niosomes have emerged as a promising nanocarrier system for targeted drug delivery, offering enhanced therapeutic efficacy and reduced systemic toxicity. This review comprehensively discusses the recent advances in the design strategies of niosomes functionalized with various ligands, polymers, and biomolecules to achieve targeted delivery to specific cells or tissues. Emphasis is placed on the molecular mechanisms underlying the improved cellular uptake, controlled release, and site-specific accumulation of drugs facilitated by surface modifications. We further explore the physicochemical parameters influencing niosome stability, targeting efficiency, and drug loading capacity. Additionally, this paper critically evaluates the preclinical and clinical progress of surface-functionalized niosomal formulations, addressing the challenges in their scalable production, regulatory considerations, and translational potential. By integrating insights from material science, molecular biology, and pharmaceutical technology, this review aims to provide a comprehensive framework for the rational design and clinical translation of surface-functionalized niosomes as next-generation targeted drug delivery platforms. Keywords: Niosomes, Targeted drug delivery, Mechanism
venue: EJPPS EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PARENTERAL AND PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCES

title: Design and exploratory assessment of a mobile educational prototype for Saraguro cultural heritage and Kichwa-language learning
abstract: Introduction Digital resources can broaden access to living heritage, but their contribution depends on cultural relevance, community governance, and claims that remain proportional to the evidence collected. This study reports the design and exploratory assessment of a mobile educational prototype focused on Saraguro cultural heritage and introductory Kichwa-language learning. The prototype organized multimedia content on gastronomy, rituals and festivals, handicrafts, ancestral medicine, stories, cultural places, and basic Kichwa expressions with audio-playback controls. It was informed by a previous project website, saragurotradiciones.site, but the two resources were technically distinct and only the mobile prototype was assessed. Methods The development process was organized through the five Mobile-D phases. An exploratory qualitative evaluation involved 12 purposively selected participants: five undergraduate students, three local tour guides, two cultural-tourism operators, and two educators. Semi-structured interviews lasted 30 -45 min, were conducted in person or by videoconference, and were recorded, transcribed, and thematically coded. Results Ten participants described the prototype as easy to navigate. Participants also valued the organization of local cultural content and georeferenced information, while identifying offline access, broader multilingual support, ex…

title: Job autonomy will set you free: how work design fosters trust and reduces prejudice beyond the workplace
abstract: Purpose This study examines how the structure of daily work shapes individuals' broader social attitudes, particularly prejudice. Design/methodology/approach Using data from the 2010 European Social Survey (ESS), we analyze a multinational sample of 12,475 respondents across 27 European countries. Findings We find that when employees experience greater autonomy in their roles, they are more likely to trust others in general and, in turn, exhibit lower levels of prejudice toward marginalized groups. However, this effect is contingent on managerial process visibility and becomes stronger when employees' effort is more difficult for managers to observe. Social implications The results demonstrate that HR practices can meaningfully influence employees' orientations toward the common good, aligning with growing calls for organizations to play a constructive role in addressing societal polarization. Originality/value The findings contribute to the prejudice literature by highlighting the importance of structural work contexts in shaping biased attitudes, to the human resource management (HRM) literature by identifying prejudice reduction as a novel outcome of job design, and to signaling theory by establishing process visibility as a key moderating factor.

title: From medical planning to spatial design: enhancing patient experience in Chinese public hospitals
abstract: Purpose Significant advances have been made in medical technology in Chinese healthcare institutions. However, the COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of inpatient living environments. Reduced hospital admissions have led to decreased revenue, thus prompting renovations for safer and more welcoming spaces. Owing to its high costs and complex scheduling, this study aims to optimize hospital interior space renovation. Design/methodology/approach Using depthMapX, DIALux and SketchUp, three enhanced spatial models (structure, lighting and color) were created for the selected hospital. A VR-based experiment was conducted with 48 former inpatients (4 groups, 12 each), who completed a five-item Light and Color Questionnaire; their task completion time was recorded. Findings Kruskal–Wallis tests and pairwise comparisons showed that the lighting-optimized model significantly improved wayfinding, safety and procedural familiarity compared to the baseline model. The structured model also showed positive effects, whereas color had the least impact. The findings provide practical guidance for Chinese public hospitals on implementing affordable interior design renovations to help restore trust among resident patients and promoting faster recovery in an enhanced environment. The study also provides an evidence-based framework for affordable hospital renovations that integrates me…
venue: Archnet-IJAR: International Journal of Architectural Research

title: Building and construction in preschool – between policy classification and children’s learning
abstract: Abstract This article explores the positioning of building and construction activities in Swedish preschool authoritative documents from the 1950s and onwards. Drawing on the concept of classification, the study analyses how these activities have shifted from being situated within the practical-aesthetic domain – closely linked to crafts and creative expression – to becoming increasingly embedded within, first the science domain, and later the technological one. The analysis reveals a recontextualisation, where building and construction activities have retained cross-disciplinary characteristics while gradually being framed as part of preschool technology education. While this shift can be understood as a strengthening of technology as a curriculum area, previous research highlights that construction activities function best as open, process‑oriented practices, where learning emerges through play, exploration, and didactical support. This creates a tension between policy‑level reclassification and the pedagogical conditions that support children’s learning, participation, and meaning‑making in building and construction activities.
venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education

title: Extending the FEA Model to Sustainable Packaging Design: The Role of Functional, Expressive, and Aesthetic Attributes in Socially Situated Consumer Experiences
abstract: Sustainable packaging design in the beauty industry must balance environmental responsibility with functional performance, expressive meaning and aesthetic appeal, yet design research has rarely examined these attributes through a framework. Drawing on the Function–Expressive–Aesthetic (FEA) model, the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) framework and social contagion theory, this study investigates how social contagion activates consumers’ functional, expressive and aesthetic needs regarding sustainable skincare packaging, and how these needs shape packaging attitudes and purchase intention. A covariance-based structural equation model was tested using survey data from consumers in markets. Results show that social contagion positively influences three FEA needs, with the strongest effect on expressive needs; expressive need fulfilment exerts the impact on packaging attitude, which in turn drives purchase intention. Findings extend the FEA model from apparel to packaging design, position social contagion as a design-diffusion mechanism, and provide evidence-based guidance for creating sustainable packaging that is environmentally responsible and socially shareable.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of the barley rhizosphere prokaryotic community following repeated inoculation with Ensifer meliloti Rm2011 in a three-year field study
abstract: Abstract Background and aims Microbial inoculants are increasingly recognized for enhancing crop productivity and sustainable agriculture. We assessed the rhizosphere competence of Ensifer meliloti Rm2011 in different barley genotypes following repeated inoculation in three growing seasons, tracking its establishment and influence on the indigenous rhizosphere prokaryotic communities. We aimed to understand how consistent field application affects prokaryotic dynamics and whether environmental conditions or plant genotype modulate its establishment within the rhizosphere community. Methods Three-year field trials evaluated the establishment of E. meliloti Rm2011 in barley rhizosphere and its impact on the prokaryotic community. Rhizosphere samples were collected at several time points throughout the vegetation period and analyzed using colony-forming units and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to further evaluate the effects of barley genotype and environmental conditions. Results E. meliloti Rm2011 demonstrated robust persistence throughout the growing season, successfully integrating into the rhizosphere community. Despite repeated inoculations, its impact on the native prokaryota was negligible across all years. Neither environmental conditions nor barley genotype had a significant effect on its establishment. Notably, a set of core bacterial taxa was consistently detected, …

title: Comparative Effects of Individual and Combined Plant-Derived Essential Oils Against the Asian Citrus Psyllid, Diaphorina citri Kuwayama (Hemiptera: Liviidae)
abstract: The Asian citrus psyllid, Diaphorina citri Kuwayama (Hemiptera: Liviidae), is a destructive insect pest of citrus crop due to direct feeding damage and indirect role in transmitting Huanglongbing disease, which infects the citrus production globally. However, limited studies were carried out on the efficacy of natural resources such as botanicals as a safe method for controlling this insect pest. We investigated the effects of three plant-based essential oils (EOs), mint, eucalyptus, and lemongrass, individually and in combination, against adult D. citri using toxicity and repellent bioassays. At 7.0% concentration and 48 hours of exposure, mint oil caused 72.8% mortality, with an LC50 of 3.17%, the lowest among all other treatments. In case of combinations of EOs, the mint+eucalyptus showed 88.9% adult mortality at 48 hours. No synergistic or antagonistic effect was recorded in all combination treatments against D. citri adult mortality. Repellency tests also revealed the strongest repellent activity of mint oil, with up to 75.6% repellency at 7.0% concentration. The repellency was further enhanced with EO combinations, where the mint + eucalyptus showed the highest repellent effect (80.6%) at 4 hours. Our findings indicate that mint oil, especially in combination with eucalyptus oil, is an effective EO to control the population of D. citri, offering a promising alternative ap…

title: Editorial: Metabolomic analysis of plant matrices: identification of compounds of therapeutic and nutraceutical interest
Limiting grain cadmium and lead accumulation in maize: foliar application of blocking agents to modulate subcellular sequestration
Knowledge graph and machine learning-guided virtual screening prioritizes putative blockers of the PSMD11/Rpn6-EBOV glycoprotein interface
abstract: Introduction Host-directed antiviral discovery requires a traceable route from host-factor identification to testable molecular hypotheses. This study developed such a workflow around a host factor associated with Ebola virus glycoprotein (EBOV GP). Methods GFP-GP pulldown coupled with co-immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry was used to identify GP-associated host candidates. A PSMD11/Rpn6-centred workflow integrated knowledge-graph inference, ligand-only machine learning, ADMETlab profiling and interface-guided docking. Candidate prioritization was assessed through score-weight sensitivity analysis, applicability-domain assessment and docking controls addressing seed reproducibility, search convergence, whole-receptor context and macrocycle ring-conformer sensitivity. Docking scores were contextualized against a matched 59-compound library. Results The analysis recovered 424 GP-pulldown-specific host proteins and nominated PSMD11/Rpn6 as a proteostasis anchor. The tier-gated knowledge-graph candidate membership was invariant across the tested weight perturbations, with Spearman rho = 0.998 under equal weighting. The selected ExtraTrees model achieved an AUC of 0.912 for the Ki endpoint. Applicability-domain assessment and ADMET profiling differentiated candidate confidence and predicted liabilities. Docking reproducibility checks yielded a maximum standard deviation of 0.05 k…

title: Scheduling interdependent HFT transactions: Managing virtual overlaps and profit timing windows through exact and approximate approaches
abstract: High-frequency trading often requires executing paired transactions within specific time intervals to capture market opportunities. To address this requirement, this study formulates this as a combinatorial optimization problem with pairing and capacity constraints. Specifically, a mixed integer programming model is proposed to maximize profits while ensuring regulatory compliance. Once the model is established, a branch-and-bound algorithm is developed to provide optimal solutions, which serve as benchmarks for assessing solution quality. However, considering the computational demands of larger instances, a hybrid genetic algorithm is further introduced to balance exploration and exploitation through selective chromosome injections and time-varying crossover and mutation rates. Computational experiments show that the branch-and-bound algorithm can serve as a benchmark for approximate algorithms. Notably, for instances of size 300, the proposed genetic algorithm achieves an average relative deviation of only 0.34 within 15 seconds. In conclusion, these results provide valuable insights for trading execution strategies, showing how operational parameters influence scheduling feasibility and profitability.

title: Sonic Verisimilitude in Virtual Heritage: Lessons from Two Decades of PLACE-Hampi
abstract: Abstract Over nearly two decades of exhibition, PLACE-Hampi has provided a rare longitudinal study in spatial audio for virtual heritage. This article examines how the project's foundational principle of sonic verisimilitude, defined as the precise correspondence between acoustic and visual space, continues to shape contemporary immersive practice. By tracing the evolution of PLACE-Hampi from its 2006 first-order Ambisonics implementation to its latest experimental recontextualization within modern game-engine environments, the study demonstrates that audiovisual coherence, rather than technological complexity or Ambisonics order alone, most informs perceptual realism and audience engagement. Drawing on field recordings, system documentation, and both quantitative and qualitative audience data, the article positions sonic verisimilitude within a broader discourse on spatial audio's role in cultural representation and curatorial practice. Emerging technologies such as AI-assisted production, real-time acoustic modeling, and personalized binaural rendering are discussed in relation to long-term preservation and ethical practice. The findings suggest that sonic verisimilitude functions not only as a technical criterion but as a design ethic and an epistemology of presence, linking sound, place, and cultural meaning across a changing technological landscape.

title: Screening gamma-induced Leucaena tarramba mutants for drought tolerance under PEG-simulated osmotic stress in hydroponics
abstract: Abstract Drought tolerance remains a major challenge in improving Leucaena tarramba, a legume widely cultivated in arid and semi-arid tropics. Effective screening for drought tolerance is critical for identifying Leucaena tarramba putative mutants with improved adaptation to water-limited environments. A hydroponic system combined with polyethylene glycol (PEG)-induced osmotic stress provides a controlled and reproducible platform for evaluating drought-related responses. This study aimed to screen M₂ mutants and identify promising drought-tolerant putative mutants based on estimated estimates of genetic variability and key morpho-physiological responses under drought-simulating osmotic stress induced by polyethylene glycol (PEG) 6000 in a hydroponic deep-water culture system. Seeds from the Livestock Breeding and Forage Crops Center, West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia were irradiated with Co-60 gamma rays at Center for Isotope and Radiation Application under the National Nuclear Energy Agency of Indonesia (PAIR-BATAN Indonesia) at doses ranging from 50 to 1000 Gy, with an estimated LD₅₀ of 820 Gy based on survival at 21 days after planting. Following phenotypic evaluation of the M₁ generation, materials derived from 0, 250, 500, and 750 Gy were advanced to the M₂ generation. A split-plot design was arranged with PEG levels consisted of 0, 10, 20% as main plot and irradiation doses …

title: Spiking Neural Network Chips for Low-Power Real-Time Edge Intelligence
abstract: Edge devices require short response time and low active and idle power, yet conventional neural-network hardware repeatedly moves weights and activations between memory and processing units. Spiking neural network (SNN) chips address this problem with event-driven communication, persistent neuron state, and local synaptic storage. This review first explains the signal path of an SNN chip through four connected modules: spike encoding, neuron computation, synaptic learning, and output decoding. It then compares three implementation routes: digital many-core platforms, mixed-signal or sensor-integrated platforms, and memristive in-memory hardware. Representative systems include TrueNorth, Loihi, Tianjic, Darwin3, ODIN, DYNAP-SE, and Speck. The comparison shows that no single metric is enough. Large digital chips provide scale and programmability but still incur memory and routing costs; mixed-signal and sensor-integrated designs reduce unnecessary activity but require attention to device mismatch and input-event rate; memristive arrays reduce weight movement but remain sensitive to variation and peripheral overhead. Meaningful evaluation therefore requires accuracy, timestep count, event activity, latency, active and idle power, and a clear measurement boundary. These criteria help identify when SNN hardware offers a practical advantage for low-power real-time edge intelligence.

title: AI knowledge capability and innovation: the power of cognitive processing and empowerment
abstract: Purpose This study aims to integrate ideas from organizational learning theory with new AI capabilities to investigate how AI-driven knowledge processes may improve innovation performance. Specifically, this study explores the process in which AI-based (AI Ba) knowledge production and integration support advancement of AI knowledge capability and AI psychological empowerment. In addition, this study also investigates the moderating role of Gen-AI cognitive. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 301 professionals in the USA working in AI-enabled organizational settings, and structural equation modeling was used for data analysis. Findings The results of this study show that both AI knowledge production Ba and AI knowledge integration Ba is positively associated with AI knowledge capability and AI psychological empowerment. AI knowledge capability is also positively related to AI innovation performance. Similarly, AI psychological empowerment is also significantly related to AI innovation performance. Furthermore, the findings of this study show that Gen-AI cognitive processing positively moderates the association between AI knowledge capability and AI innovation performance, while Gen-AI cognitive processing did not moderate the relationship between AI psychological empowerment and AI innovation performance. Originality/value Overall, this study contributes to the…

title: Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control for Single-Stage Isolated Bidirectional V2G Chargers
abstract: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology plays a critical role in modern power systems by utilizing electric vehicles as distributed energy storage to smooth power fluctuations and achieve peak-shaving and valley-filling. As a vital power electronics interface, single-stage isolated bidirectional AC/DC converters offer significant advantages in high power density and electrical isolation. However, conventional control methods often suffer from sluggish dynamic response and insufficient robustness when subjected to parameter uncertainties and external disturbances. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved super-twisting sliding mode control (STA) strategy integrated with a low-pass filter. The proposed strategy effectively suppresses inherent chattering while retaining the strong robustness characteristic of traditional sliding mode control. Simulation results demonstrate that the control strategy maintains superior dynamic performance and robustness under external noise interference and variations in battery internal resistance, offering a highly effective solution for high-performance power conversion in V2G systems.
venue: Power Electronics Research and Applications Transactions

Efficacy of plant extracts for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a network meta-analysis
abstract: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide, affecting approximately 38% of the global population. This network meta-analysis systematically compared the effects of different plant extracts on liver biochemical and non-invasive histological outcomes in patients with MASLD. Methods This study was performed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251229711). We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science up to November 12, 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing plant extracts in adults with MASLD. Primary outcomes were alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), liver stiffness measurement (LSM), and hepatic steatosis percentage. Network meta-analyses were conducted using Stata 15.1 and R 4.2.1. Results In total, 32 RCTs were included, involving 2,053 patients and 28 types of plant extracts. For liver enzyme outcomes, a novel curcumin preparation (CP) exhibited the highest ranking probability for ALT reduction (SUCRA: 91.93%), whereas cinnamon (Cin) ranked highest for AST reduction (SUCRA: 88.48%). For non-invasive histological outcomes, purslane (Pur) showed the greatest ranking probability for reducing LSM (SUCRA: 94.16%), while fenugreek (Fen) dem…

title: Genetic evaluation of bioactive compounds and mineral nutrients in bitter gourd (Momordica charantia L.) using heterosis and combining ability approach
Study of hydrophobic coatings and potential water savings in solar power plants
abstract: This study explores the challenges related to dust deposition on solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Review of earlier works suggests solar PV performance is significantly affected by the dust deposition and the power loss can vary from 10% to more than 60% in some cases depending on the location. Hydrophobic coatings can offer a potential pathway for reducing dust deposition and water saving in cleaning operations. This paper presents the comparative study of the four commercially available and one developed silica-based hydrophobic coating to estimate the quantity of the water required for cleaning of the dust. Comparative experimental tests reveal that the developed coating has the highest contact angle (145°), least contact angle hysteresis (5°) and least surface free energy (17.4 mN/m) as compared to the other coatings. The prepared coating slightly decreased the visible light transmittance of the glass from 92.4% to 90.23%. The water saving with the hydrophobic coatings is found to be in the range 28%–55%; the highest water saving is observed with the developed coating as it is almost near to a superhydrophobic coating in behaviour. Furthermore, the scope for future work and challenges related to the development and use of hydrophobic coatings in the solar area are discussed.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Energy

title: Commercial Ambition and State Power of the British East India Company: The Rise of the "Company-State"
abstract: The British East India Company presents a typical case of the fusion between commercial expansion and state power in the history of the British Empire. The Company was initially established to secure a commercial monopoly, but its objectives were gradually converted to the de facto domination of South Asia. This paper examines the principal stages and mechanisms through which the EIC was transformed from a commercial enterprise into a "Company-State." Specifically, the first stage, from its foundation in 1600 to 1660, explores its basic form as a commercial company and the initial political interactions with Indian polities during the construction of the trading network. The second stage, from 1660 to 1765, focuses on the establishment of its military forces and rivalry with France in South India, with the result of pivotal control over Bengal. The third stage, from approximately 1765 to 1800, analyses how, after obtaining the Diwani (revenue-collecting rights), the Company constructed administrative, fiscal and judicial systems, completing the institutional transition from commercial monopolist to territorial ruler.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: When the algorithm decides: moral legitimacy, ethical bank managers, and the restorative power of territorial embeddedness
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine associations between ethical leadership (EL), algorithmic transparency, perceived algorithmic authority (PAA) and employee moral confidence (EMC) in digitally mediated banking. It explores whether territorial embeddedness (TE) supports the reconstruction of human moral legitimacy when decisions are mediated by algorithmic systems. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods design was used. In the qualitative phase, two focus groups with rural and urban bank managers were conducted to refine the proposed Algorithmic Moral Displacement Theory (AMDT) framework and adapt measurement items to banking contexts. The quantitative phase tested the model using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with data from 606 managers and employees in 79 bank offices in Extremadura, Spain, including 44 rural and 35 urban/semi-urban offices. Mediation and multi-group analysis compared territorial contexts and respondent roles. Findings Perceived moral autonomy of leadership emerged as an intervening mechanism linking EL, algorithmic authority, transparency and TE with EMC. PAA was not directly associated with moral confidence but operated through employees’ evaluations of managerial ethical interpretation. TE was positively associated with managerial moral autonomy and EMC, particularly in rural settings, whereas urban results emphasized tr…
venue: International Journal of Ethics and Systems

title: Challenges and future outlooks towards mitigating water pollution from crude oil refinery plant
abstract: As part of the UN Sustainable Development Goals 2020 emphasising the need for clean water and sanitation, it is imperative that all wastewater from a refinery plant should be adequately treated to safeguard our environment from toxic pollutants. Globally, the volume of petroleum refinery wastewater (PRWW) usually generated is approximately 1.6 times the crude oil volume processed in a refinery. This paper critically reviews the existing treatment methodologies and their fundamental challenges. In addition, it highlights the future prospects of zero liquid discharge (ZLD) reverse osmosis systems powered by renewable energy. The adopted methodology involves searching online for relevant keywords on water pollution from a crude oil refinery plant in scientific databases. About 347 articles were downloaded, out of which 122 were utilised for the review exercise. The possibility of achieving a 5.8% reduction in energy consumption on a global basis while processing 2000 l of PRWW per day using 5.04 kW of solar energy for 10 h with the aid of ZLD-reverse osmosis is presented. Also, energy and treatment costs can be reduced by 58%–75% and 48%–67%, respectively. By adopting sustainable and innovative approaches, crude oil refineries can significantly reduce their environmental footprint, align with global sustainability goals, and ensure compliance with regulatory standards.

title: Wireless Power Transfer Technology Based on Magnetic Coupling Resonance
abstract: With the rapid development of modern technology, smart wireless devices have been widely used in daily life and industrial production, putting forward a clear demand for reliable wireless power supply solutions. Among existing technologies, magnetic coupling resonance has become an important choice for low-to-medium power applications because it achieves a good balance between transmission distance and efficiency. This paper presents a systematic review of magnetic coupling resonant wireless power transfer technology, covering the basic working principles, current research status, existing limitations and future development directions. First, the basic principles of magnetic resonant coupling wireless power transfer are introduced. Then, discussions are carried out from three core research directions: coupling mechanism design, mutual inductance calculation methods and parameter optimization techniques, and representative works on closed, open and semi-open coil structures, analytical mutual inductance models and intelligent optimization algorithms are reviewed in turn. The paper points out two main shortcomings of current research: the lack of studies on multi-coil relay systems and the insufficient analysis of actual operating conditions. Finally, this paper sorts out future research directions worth paying attention to, in order to promote the technology from laboratory envi…

title: Simulation-Based Basic Life Support Learning Through Peer Education: A Quasi-Experimental Study
abstract: Nursing education must continue to be developed in Indonesia, laboratory learning methods are an important thing that is still an issue today. Some obstacles faced when students go to the clinic are poor student skills, practicum hours, the number of laboratory assistants, and appropriate learning methods to practice clinical skills in the laboratory. This study aims to analyze the skills and abilities of handling Basic Life Support (BLS) in nursing students using peer education and simulation methods. The study used a Quasy-experimental design with a pre- and post-experimental design, sampling using the Consecutive Sampling technique with a total of 60 nursing students with inclusion criteria. The instruments used in the study used Standard Operating Procedures and BLS Practicum Checklist sheets and knowledge instruments about BLS with validity and reliability test results using Cronbach's alpha > 0.70, Practicum tools used phantom and AED Simulator. The results of the study are there is an increase in student knowledge and competence using simulation with peer education methods after intervention. Discussions with mutual interaction in practicums using peer methods make students more challenged to always learn and increase motivation to carry out practicums independently with the help of peers.
venue: Medical Technology and Public Health Journal

title: Peer navigation to support psychosocial well-being and HIV treatment among adolescents: A rapid review
abstract: Background: Adolescents living with HIV (ALHIV) in sub-Saharan Africa experience poorer outcomes across the HIV care cascade than other age groups because of intersecting developmental, psychosocial and structural barriers. Peer navigation has emerged as a promising strategy to support engagement in care, yet evidence on its effectiveness and implementation for ALHIV remains fragmented. Aim: To synthesise evidence on peer navigation and peer-led psychosocial support interventions for adolescents living with HIV. Method: A rapid review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 principles. PubMed and EBSCOhost databases were searched for qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods studies published between 2013 and 2025. Results: Fourteen studies conducted across eight countries were included. Peer navigation interventions were typically delivered by young adults living with HIV who were stable on treatment and trained to provide psychosocial, adherence and health system navigation support. Most studies reported improvements in antiretroviral therapy adherence, retention in care and viral suppression, although effects varied by context and were not always sustained. Psychosocial benefits included reduced stigma, strengthened trust and improved self-efficacy. Implementation findings indicated high acceptability and feasibility, supported by structured training and supervision, …

title: Inclusive leadership as the missing infrastructure: reframing peer support worker withdrawal as a failure of belonging
abstract: Purpose This viewpoint aims to challenge the prevailing assumption in mental health service literature that peer support worker (PSW) disengagement and turnover are primarily workforce-management problems, solvable through clearer job descriptions, certification and pay. It argues instead that PSW withdrawal is frequently a leadership failure: organisations formally invite peer workers into clinical structures without leaders doing the relational work of including them. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on leader inclusiveness theory, the workplace inclusion model and qualitative evidence on the occupational identity of PSWs, this viewpoint distinguishes between the structural inclusion organisations claim (policy commitments, job titles, headcount targets) and the relational inclusion peer workers actually experience day-to-day from their leaders and teams. Findings PSWs already occupy a liminal occupational identity, suspended between lived experience and clinical professionalism. Where leaders fail to convert structural inclusion into everyday relational inclusion, this liminality curdles into a self-protective withdrawal here termed Liminal Exile: peer workers remain procedurally compliant and outwardly present while quietly disengaging from the disclosure and relational risk-taking that justified their employment in the first place. This withdrawal is frequently misread …

title: Peer influence in juvenile offending: social evaluation, relational identity and moral obligation
abstract: Purpose Although peer influence is widely recognized as important in juvenile offending, less is known about how justice-involved adolescents themselves interpret peer evaluation, understand their roles within peer relationships and make sense of their responsibilities in peer-related offending situations. This study aims to explore these relational meanings in adolescents’ accounts of offending. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on semistructured interviews with 18 justice-involved adolescents in China, this study used thematic analysis, informed by abductive reasoning, to examine how participants understood peer influence in relation to their offending. Findings The analysis identified three analytically distinct but overlapping dimensions of peer influence: social evaluation sensitivity, relational identity commitment and group-based moral obligation. Participants described how concerns about peer acceptance, rejection and reputation shaped their responses to peer expectations; how friendships became connected to their sense of identity and belonging; and how involvement in offending was sometimes understood as helping, protecting, repaying or supporting peers. Practical implications The findings may inform future assessment research by highlighting adolescents’ interpretations of peer rejection, friendship obligations and responsibility in peer-related offending. title: Assessing Peer Collaboration Strategies Among Senior High School Teachers at Sulu College of Technology, Incorporated
abstract: This study assessed the extent of peer collaboration strategies employed by senior high school teachers at Sulu College of Technology, Incorporated. Specifically, it examined peer collaboration in terms of sharing teaching strategies and best practices, joint lesson planning and curriculum development, peer mentoring and coaching, and professional support and teamwork. The study also determined the relationship between peer collaboration strategies and the demographic characteristics of the respondents. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed involving 100 senior high school teacher-respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using frequency counts, percentages, weighted mean, standard deviation, Pearson product-moment correlation, independent samples t-test, and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The findings revealed that most of the respondents were 40 years old or younger, female, married, had fewer than five years of teaching experience, and held a bachelor’s degree. Overall, the extent of peer collaboration strategies across the four domains was rated as "Often," indicating that collaborative practices were regularly implemented among the teachers. Respondents who were female, aged 31–40 years, married, held a master’s degree, and had 6–10 years of teaching experience reported more favourabl…
venue: The International Review of Multidisciplinary Research

title: Anion-participating solvation enables compositionally graded interphases for durable subzero lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Low-temperature operation remains a critical bottleneck for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), since the coupled limitations in Li<sup>+</sup> transport, desolvation and interfacial stability severely undermine energy delivery and long-term cyclability. Here, rather than merely relying on low-freezing-point solvents to improve electrolyte fluidity, we design a lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB)-based electrolyte combining fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), dimethyl sulfite (DMS) and 1,1,2,2-Tetrafluoroethyl-2,2,2-trifluoroethyl ether (HFE) to simultaneously regulate the solvation structure and interfacial reactions under subzero conditions. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the LiDFOB + DMS/HFE/FEC electrolyte reconstructs the Li<sup>+</sup> solvation sheath from solvent-dominated coordination in LiPF<sub>6</sub> + ethylene carbonate/dimethyl carbonate to an anion-dominated, aggregate-rich structure. Sputtering-time-dependent X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a compositionally graded graphite solid electrolyte interphase in which LiF remains the predominant fluorine-containing species and the relative contribution of Li-O-containing species increases with continued sputtering, while total-ion-normalized time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry provides complementary semiquantitative trends for selected interphase fragments. A compositionally differentiated h…

Covalent Organic Frameworks in Energy Storage Devices
abstract: With the aim of carbon neutrality, there are serious problems in the supply of lithium resources and inherent safety risks of traditional lithium-ion batteries that are hindering the green development of the energy-storage industry. Porous Crystalline Polymers with tailored structures called Covalent Organic Frameworks (COFs) have been developed to address various problems in industry. Two general synthetic Strategies are given. Traditional solvothermal synthesis of COF powders has good crystallinity but is energy-intensive and produces a large amount of pollutants. Electrochemical Polymerisation is a relatively simple way to prepare flexible COF thin films. Modifying the pore channel and active site of functionalised COFs to build single-ion solid-state electrolytes with high room-temperature ionic conductivity and suppress the growth of lithium dendrites has been achieved. Long-cycle lithium-ion battery anodes have been prepared by covalent bonding with MXene; redox-active COFs are also good supercapacitor materials. Polyimide COF films can also be employed in energy storage and electrochromism for the development of flexible wearable energy-storage devices. Although they have a low intrinsic electrical conductivity, COFs are still used in some places. By reasonably modifying the molecule and regulating the interface, it will be a good material for the next generation of high…

title: Energy-efficient multimodal motion control of hybrid underwater gliders based on an optimized model predictive active disturbance rejection framework
abstract: Hybrid Underwater Glider (HUG) serve as critical platforms for extended and large-scale ocean observations. However, achieving precise trajectory tracking in complex and dynamic marine environment, remains a significant challenge. This paper addresses the multimodal trajectory tracking problem for HUG by proposing a composite control framework integrating Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC), Model Predictive Control (MPC), and Adaptive Line-of-Sight (ALOS). First, a six-degree-of-freedom dynamic model is established, ALOS is designed to achieve decoupling and smooth guidance of horizontal and vertical motions by dynamically adjusting the look-ahead distance and depth-pitch coupling mechanism. Second, an Extended State Observer (ESO) was validated for real-time estimation of total system disturbances. MPC replaced the conventional Nonlinear Law State Error Feedback (NLSEF), utilizing rolling optimization strategies to address actuator physical constraints and state constraints, thereby enhancing the predictive capability and robustness of the controller. Finally, the framework’s performance was validated through multimodal task simulations. Simulation results demonstrate that this framework significantly outperforms traditional methods. During trajectory tracking, horizontal tracking error is maintained within 3 meters, depth deviation is reduced to 0.52 meters. In the c…

title: Electrochemical Structural Dynamics of Transparent Capacitive Ion Storage Electrodes for Electrochromic Polymer Displays
abstract: Abstract Transparent capacitive ion storage layers are essential for electrochromic devices (ECDs) because they determine charge balance, electrochemical switching kinetics, optical neutrality, and bistability. However, their electrochemical structural dynamics and their relationship with ECD performance remain insufficiently understood compared with that of the active electrochromic material itself. Here, we investigate nanoengineered indium tin oxide (ITO) nanoparticles and PEDOT:PSS as transparent capacitive ion storage layers for p-type polymer-based ECDs. ITO nanoparticles show robust, optically neutral double-layer capacitance for fast ECD responses with high coloration efficiency, whereas PEDOT:PSS exhibits pseudocapacitive mixed ionic/electronic transport with pronounced optical memory. By combining electrochemical analysis on morphological and crystalline dynamics, we reveal that ITO nanoparticles maintain stable morphology and crystallinity, while PEDOT:PSS undergoes electrochemically induced lamellar densification without surface degradation during electrochemical operation. PEDOT:PSS is further utilized as a capacitive transparent working electrode after polar-solvent vapor annealing, which provides high electrical conductivity and a mixed-conducting capacitive interface adjacent to the electrochromic polymers. When combined with interfacial charge-buffering PEDOT:P…

title: Equivalent Time Inference for Left-Truncated Degradation Data with Unknown Storage History in Accelerated Degradation Modeling
abstract: In accelerated degradation tests of highly reliable products, newly manufactured samples are often scarce, while historical inventories contain naturally aged units with unknown storage histories and left-truncated data. To address this issue, an equivalent time transformation method is proposed to integrate pre-storage degradation with accelerated test data. The degradation of new samples is modeled using a nonlinear Wiener process, with parameters estimated via Bayesian MCMC. The equivalent aging time of stored samples is inferred by maximizing the probability density function, enabling temporal alignment across heterogeneous data sources. The transformed data are then incorporated to reconstruct lifetime distributions. Validation using photomultiplier tube (PMT) data and leave-one-out cross-validation shows reduced RMSE and MAPE. The results demonstrate improved data utilization, enhanced estimation stability, and more accurate reliability prediction under small-sample conditions.
venue: International Journal of Reliability, Quality and Safety Engineering

title: Recent Advances in Supercapacitors: Charge-Storage Mechanisms, Electrode Materials, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Supercapacitors are valued for rapid power delivery and exceptional cycling endurance, yet increasing the energy stored per unit mass or volume remains difficult. The three representative device configurations in this review are electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs) based on interfacial ion adsorption, pseudo capacitors that use fast redox or intercalation reactions, and hybrid systems combining both storage modes. Recent progress in the performance of carbon electrodes has focused on creating pores for electrolyte ion access, building continuous transport paths and modifying surface chemistry, rather than increasing the nominal surface area. Redox-active electrodes, such as transition-metal compounds, conjugated polymers, and MXenes and related two-dimensional carbides/nitrides, can store a large amount of charge but often have slow electron transfer kinetics, structural instability and increased interfacial resistance during cycling. A hybrid structure can be used to combine energy storage and power delivery, provided that the two electrodes can operate at the same speed and potential, and the electrolyte is stable in the operating environment. Therefore, future development will move beyond individual material modifications to device-level co-design. The main demands are atomic-level control of the electrode-electrolyte interface, electrolytes with wide electrochemical and…

title: R&D or marketing? The choice for a battery electric vehicle supply chain under dual credits policy
abstract: Purpose This study examines how China's dual-credit policy shapes research and development (R&D) and marketing choices in a battery electric vehicle (BEV) supply chain and identifies when different strategy combinations are preferred. Design/methodology/approach We develop a Stackelberg game with one BEV manufacturer and one seller. The manufacturer chooses driving-range-oriented R&D or quality-oriented improvement and sets the wholesale price. The seller then decides whether to undertake marketing and sets the retail price. Demand depends on price, driving range, quality, and marketing effort, while the policy is represented by the credit trading price and a range-related credit rule. Findings Both R&D strategies expand BEV demand, and marketing amplifies this effect. However, high marketing sensitivity can induce costly effort and tighter margins, making the seller better off foregoing marketing and free riding on demand generated by the manufacturer's improvement. Quality improvement is preferred when the credit price or range sensitivity is low. Otherwise, range-oriented R&D is optimal. The credit trading price directly reshapes the manufacturer's improvement choice and can also affect the seller's marketing threshold under driving-range-oriented R&D. Research limitations/implications To keep the manufacturer + seller interaction under the dual-credit policy as transparent …
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Battery Electrode Design Process Using Deep Neural Network
abstract: Abstract The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) demands lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) customized for diverse energy and power density requirements, yet the intricate trade-offs among electrode design parameters make conventional trial-and-error optimization costly and time-consuming. This study presents the battery electrode exploration network (BattleNet), a deep learning model that predicts the specific capacity across multiple C-rates, collectively representing the rate capability, from electrode design parameters, including loading level, thickness, and porosity. Trained entirely on real-world experimental data, BattleNet achieved an R2 of 0.889, outperforming conventional machine learning baselines. Based on these predictions, an inverse design framework was proposed to explore design parameters satisfying a target rate capability. The explored parameters matched the target with an average error of 7.9%, and cells fabricated within the explored region satisfied the target performance with an average error of merely 4.5%. These results demonstrate the practical feasibility of deep learning as a tool to accelerate LIB design and development for the EV industry.
