title: SOCIAL ACCEPTANCE OF LOW-EMISSION PUBLIC TRANSPORT DEVELOPMENT AS AN INVESTMENT PRIORITY IN THE CORE CITY OF THE POZNAŃ AGGLOMERATION
abstract: The aim of the study was to assess the level of social acceptance of low-emission public transport development as an investment priority for Poznań, the core city of the Poznań agglomeration, and to identify the main factors associated with this acceptance. The empirical material consisted of data from a survey conducted in the second half of 2025 among 515 Poznań residents aged 16-75. Descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression were applied. The results showed that nearly 60% of respondents supported the development of low-emission public transport as an investment priority for the city. Higher odds of acceptance were significantly associated with respondents’ age, the importance they attached to CO₂ emissions when choosing a mode of transport, and their assessment of the extent to which residents’ opinions were taken into account in the investment planning process. The remaining socio-demographic and mobility-related characteristics included in the analysis were not significantly associated with the level of acceptance. The findings highlight the importance of the social dimension of local transport transition. Alongside infrastructural and technological solutions, the environmental aspects of residents’ transport choices and their perceptions of how public opinion is incorporated into investment planning also play an important role.<…

title: Transport Limitation Induced by Electron-Electron Interaction in Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Films
abstract: Abstract One-dimensional conductors, such as single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs), offer an excellent platform for investigating the dimensionality-related effects. In this work, we demonstrate that the non-Drude behavior observed in the far-infrared spectra of SWNT films is a direct manifestation of electron-electron interactions characteristic of one-dimensional transport. Our results reveal a linear frequency dependence of the electron relaxation rate, in agreement with predictions from Tomonaga-Luttinger theory. Employing a modified microscopic model, we describe the conductivity spectra of SWNT films across the entire optical range and derive the theoretical lower bound for their dc sheet resistance. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the physics of one-dimensional materials and offer valuable insights for the development of SWNT-based transparent electrodes.

title: Global dispersal of macroalgae-derived recalcitrant DOC may substantially contribute to deep-ocean carbon storage
abstract: Macroalgae, the dominant primary producers of Earth’s most productive coastal vegetated ecosystems and a vital component driving ocean carbon sequestration, produce ∼5 to 80% of their net primary productivity as dissolved organic carbon (DOC). However, the global extent, fate, and contribution of this macroalgae-derived DOC to the pelagic carbon pool remain poorly understood. We establish a molecular fingerprint of the dominant coastal macroalga Saccharina japonica –derived DOC (kelp-derived DOC) using ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry and conservative filtering. We differentiate the kelp-derived DOC into labile (LDOC) and recalcitrant fractions (RDOC) based on prolonged resistance to microbial degradation, identify discriminating molecular traits through machine learning, and integrate them into a stability metric, molecular recalcitrance score (MRS). Both candidate kelp-associated RDOC signals and the more persistent, semilabile subset of candidate kelp-associated LDOC signals are detected throughout the global ocean, as far as ∼10,000 kilometers from kelp ecosystems and at depths of ∼5500 meters. Detected candidate kelp-associated DOC signals exhibit elevated MRS, with values positively correlated with distance from source regions, indicating selective long-distance transport of intrinsically more stable compounds. PUBLIC SUPPORT AND COSTS OF GHG EMISSION REDUCTION IN THE UNITED ARAB EMIRATES
abstract: This study examined the factors influencing public support for costly greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation policies in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), an oil-dependent economy in which about 89% of the population are transient residents. An on-line survey collected responses from 1,540 respondents in 2021. The sample was applied to estimate the empirical relationship using ordered logit regression and results allowed calculations of the probability change in the support of costly mitigation programs (the latent dependent variable). Results identify agreement with statements about climate-related ideas as the strongest predictors of policy support. Statements such as: “the world’s climate is changing”, “UAE temperatures will rise”, “the balance of nature is delicate,” and “lower oil prices will reduce household income” are associated with support for costly mitigation. Among socio-demographic characteristics, Filipino and Indian respondents – the two largest expatriate groups – show significantly lower support than other expatriates, while Christian respondents and higher-income respondents signal greater support than respondents indicating other religious affiliations or less income.

title: Enhancing Sensitivity of Atmospheric Pressure Laser Ablation Carbon Fiber Ionization Mass Spectrometry Imaging for Endogenous Metabolites Using a Polydopamine/Covalent Organic Framework Composite
abstract: Abstract The spatial distribution of endogenous small-molecule metabolites is pivotal for understanding living processes, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic principles. However, achieving high-sensitivity spatial metabolomic profiling remains challenging for atmospheric pressure mass spectrometry imaging (AP-MSI) due to low desorption/ionization efficiency, leading to the systematic omission of low-abundance yet biologically vital metabolites from spatial maps. Here, we developed a high-sensitivity MSI platform that integrated a polydopamine/covalent organic framework (PDA/COF) composite substrate with atmospheric pressure laser ablation carbon fiber ionization (LACFI) technology for spatial mapping of endogenous small-molecule metabolites in biological tissues. This substrate employed a polydopamine (PDA) interlayer to guide the ordered assembly of a COF on the substrate. The resulting PDA/COF composite substrate exhibited uniform surface coverage, strong stability, and excellent light absorption, collectively improving the laser desorption/ionization efficiency of metabolites. Moreover, the substrate was simple, easy to use, and cost-effective. Our platform demonstrated a significantly enhanced sensitivity, achieving an improvement of more than 2-fold based on the slope of the linear calibration curve for analysis of metabolites compared with MALDI, DESI, LACFI using copper-…

title: Electrochemical Detection of Penicillin G Using a Nanomolecularly Imprinted Polymer Sensor Modified with Carbon Nanofibers and Gold Nanowires
abstract: Abstract This study explores the electrochemical behavior of nanomolecularly imprinted polymers (NMIPs) integrated with carbon nanofibers (CNFs) and gold nanowires (AuNWs) modified on screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCEs) using cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and differential pulse voltammetry for the determination of penicillin G. The incorporation of CNFs and AuNWs enhanced electron transfer and improved the electrocatalytic performance of the modified sensor. NMIPs act as artificial biomarkers that selectively bind to the target analyte, penicillin G. Bare and modified SPCEs were characterized using [Fe(CN)6]3–/4– as a redox probe in 1 M KCl. The chemical composition and surface morphology of the nanomaterials were further characterized using field-emission scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray diffraction analysis. The CNFs/AuNWs/SPCE-modified sensor showed a 2.35-fold increase in current compared with the bare electrode. The fabricated CNFs/AuNWs/NMIPs/SPCE sensor demonstrated a strong linear response over the range of 0.001–30 μM (R2 = 0.9892), with a detection limit of 1.0 nM. Furthermore, the sensor exhibited excellent selectivity toward penicillin G, along with good reproducibility (1.14%), stability, and satisfactory recovery rates (92%–98%) in pharmaceutical pr…

title: Extreme climate shocks and agricultural net carbon sinks: the moderating role of supply chain resilience in China
abstract: Introduction Extreme climate shocks increasingly challenge the ability of agricultural systems to sustain crop carbon fixation while controlling production-related emissions. Methods Using panel data for 240 Chinese cities from 2002 to 2023, this study examines the relationships between four climate shocks—extreme high temperature (HTD), extreme low temperature (LTD), extreme rainfall (ERD), and extreme drought (EED)—and agricultural net carbon sinks (NCS), together with the moderating role of agricultural supply chain resilience. NCS is measured as annual crop-biomass carbon fixation net of selected agricultural production emissions, thereby providing an integrated, production-based indicator of agricultural carbon performance. Results Two-way fixed-effects estimates show that all four climate shocks are negatively associated with NCS, and the direction of these relationships remains stable across alternative accounting boundaries, sample adjustments, leave-one-province-out tests, and double machine learning specifications. Agricultural supply chain resilience significantly conditions the climate–carbon relationship. Its resistance, recovery, and reorientation capacities attenuate the adverse associations of high-temperature, extreme-rainfall, and drought shocks with NCS. The low-temperature result further indicates that the effectiveness of resilience depends on matching supp…

title: Long-Lived Polarization Memory from Piezoelectric Electron-Acoustic Phonon Coupling in Symmetric Spherical-like Cesium Lead Bromide Nanocrystals
abstract: Abstract The anisotropic nature of halide perovskite nanostructures gives rise to intriguing polarized optical transitions. While shape-induced anisotropy in halide perovskites is well-documented, the role of intrinsic structural symmetry remains elusive. Using symmetric spherical-like cesium lead bromide nanocrystals to isolate shape effects, we correlate intrinsic symmetry with polarized optical transitions via polarization-selective ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy and 8-band k·p modeling. We demonstrate that polarization anisotropy in an ensemble of photoexcited perovskite nanocrystals arises from transition dipole moment asymmetry inherent to the orthorhombic structure. This anisotropy persists for ∼2 ps─exceeding conventional semiconductors─owing to piezoelectric electron-transverse acoustic phonon coupling, which results in an unusual temperature dependence following τ ∝ T–0.6. Furthermore, the anisotropy amplitude and lifetime show a strong size dependence driven by internal shear strain. Reducing the nanocrystal size enhances the shear strain, leading to a concomitant enhancement in both the anisotropy amplitude and lifetime. Collectively, our findings provide deep insights into the role of intrinsic structural symmetry in polarized transitions, which is crucial for engineering polarization-sensitive perovskite light-emitting devices.

title: NT-proBNP–echocardiographic discordance in type 2 diabetes: links with adiposity and left atrioventricular coupling
abstract: Background NT-proBNP is widely used to support the exclusion of heart failure, but its concentration may be lower in individuals with excess adiposity and insulin resistance. Whether NT-proBNP below 125 pg/mL excludes early echocardiographic abnormalities in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains uncertain. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 191 adults with T2DM hospitalized between May 2024 and November 2025. NT-proBNP measurement and echocardiography were performed within 48 hours. NT-proBNP was categorized at 125 pg/mL and compared with two prespecified echocardiographic outcomes: Layer 1, an operational definition of diastolic dysfunction informed by the 2025 American Society of Echocardiography recommendations and based on consistently available variables; and Layer 2, a composite structural and/or diastolic abnormality. Associations of body mass index (BMI) and the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) with left atrial and atrioventricular coupling phenotypes were assessed among participants with NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL. Results Among the 191 participants, 153 had NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL. Layer 1 abnormality was present in 17 of these participants (11.1%), whereas Layer 2 abnormality was present in 38 (24.8%). Agreement between NT-proBNP classification and Layer 1 and Layer 2 outcomes was 79.6% (Cohen κ=0.326) and 73.3% (Cohen κ=0.328), re…

title: Near-Unity Energy Transfer from Triplet to Self-Trapped Excitons in Transparent Hybrid Metal Halide Glasses for High-Resolution X-ray Imaging
abstract: Abstract Hybrid metal halides are promising scintillators due to their strong X-ray absorption and efficient self-trapped exciton (STE) emission. However, their practical applications are largely hindered by poor processability, severe light scattering, and substantial energy loss during secondary electron relaxation, leading to low spatial resolution in X-ray imaging. Here, we report a solvent-assisted rapid evaporation method for fabricating a class of hybrid metal halide glasses with excellent processability and high optical transparency. A molecular design strategy is further introduced by incorporating triphenylphosphonium-based organic phosphorescent cations to effectively reclaim the energy dissipated during the relaxation of secondary electrons. In addition to the direct X-ray excitation of the inorganic STE state, the harvested triplet excitons can further sensitize STE emission with near-unity energy transfer efficiency. This dual-sensitization pathway synergistically enhances the scintillation performance. A large-area scintillation screen is successfully fabricated, achieving high-resolution X-ray imaging with a spatial resolution of 22.5 lp mm–1.

Religion, Identity, and Belonging: Protestant Christianity and Everyday Social Integration among East African Protestants in Finland
abstract: Finnish integration policies increasingly emphasize secular civic participation, yet Protestant Christianity remains central to how East African migrants navigate Finnish society. Drawing on twenty-four in-depth interviews with Kenyan, Ugandan, and Tanzanian Protestants and participant observation in three Helsinki congregations spanning the Pentecostal, Evangelical, and Anglican traditions, this article demonstrates that the relationship between religion and integration is dimension-specific rather than uniform. Protestant churches operate as mediating institutions that facilitate the social, cultural, and identity dimensions of integration. They provide belonging, dignity-affirming theological frameworks, and dense networks of mutual support, and shape civic-political participation in theologically contingent ways. At the same time, Protestant churches offer only limited leverage over structural integration into labor and housing markets, where racialized discrimination constrains outcomes regardless of migrants’ religious or individual resources. The article moves beyond the question of whether immigrant religion is a “bridge or barrier” to inclusion by demonstrating that the same religious community can simultaneously be both. The study extends scholarship on African diaspora Christianity, which has concentrated overwhelmingly on West African churches in Britain, Germany, a…

THE IMPORTANCE OF RENEWABLE ENERGY PRODUCTION IN EUROPEAN UNION FARMS, 2004-2023
abstract: The growing importance of renewable energy sources in the European economy has increased interest in the role of farms as energy producers. The aim of this study was to assess the scale of renewable energy production in farms across the European Union and to identify the factors affecting its level. The analysis covers the period 2004-2023 and is based on data from the Farm Sustainability Data Network (FSDN), formerly the Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN). The study examined the value of renewable energy production and other gainful activities directly related to the holding (SE730), the share of this category in total farm output, and the extent to which energy costs were covered. In addition, differences in the analysed indicators among EU Member States were assessed. Panel data models were applied to identify the determinants of renewable energy production. The findings highlight the importance of renewable energy production within the overall economic activity of EU farms and identify the main factors fostering its development. These include utilised agricultural area, total output, and total assets. The direction and magnitude of these effects varied according to farm size. The results indicate a gradual increase in the importance of energy-related activities in EU farms; however, their overall scale remains relatively limited.

title: Testing Narrow-jet Gamma-Ray Bursts as Sources of Ultrahigh-Energy Cosmic Rays
abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) have long been considered candidate sources of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) due to their large energy release and relativistic outflows. The detection of multi-TeV γ rays from GRB 221009A and its rarity have renewed interest in this connection and motivate considering an additional narrow-jet long GRB population in the local Universe. We investigate whether such a local narrow-jet population can contribute to the observed diffuse UHECR energy spectrum. We also examine the associated cosmogenic neutrino and cascade γ-ray emissions to assess the multimessenger viability of this scenario. We fit the observed UHECR spectrum and mass composition data using three source-evolution models: a uniform comoving source emissivity, a standard-jet GRB population tracing the star formation rate (SFR), and a standard + narrow jet GRB population tracing SFR. We propagate a mixed-composition UHECR injection and calculate the cosmogenic neutrino and cascade γ-ray fluxes. The standard + narrow jet model fits the observed UHECR spectrum and composition, with the highest-energy flux dominated by the narrow-jet population confined to złe z_ This low-redshift dominance lowers the cosmogenic neutrino flux compared to the standard-jet GRB population. title: Integration of AI-driven ultrasound and molecular testing to improve diagnosis of indeterminate thyroid nodules
abstract: Background Indeterminate thyroid nodules (Bethesda III/IV) are difficult to manage: ultrasound and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) often yield non-definitive results, so many patients undergo diagnostic lobectomy for lesions that prove benign. The combination of AI-enhanced ultrasound and molecular biomarker platforms provides complementary diagnostic capabilities. However, evidence on their combined application remains limited, derives from a small number of early studies, and has not yet been validated in large or prospective cohorts. Methods A systematic search of PubMed (2012–2025) identified studies evaluating the diagnostic performance of conventional ultrasound + FNA, AI-assisted ultrasound, molecular biomarker platforms (Afirma, ThyroSeq, ThyGeNEXT, ThyraMIR), and integrated multimodal approaches combining AI-enhanced ultrasound radiomics with molecular biomarker testing in indeterminate thyroid nodules. The search was limited to English-language publications. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 49 studies were included. Extracted outcomes included sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), and positive predictive value (PPV). Study quality was appraised using QUADAS-2, and model reporting transparency was benchmarked against TRIPOD and STARD-AI guidelines. Because of methodological heterogeneity, no meta-analysis or statistical pooling was per…

title: Smart cold storage control using fruit identification for energy-efficient refrigeration
abstract: Abstract Optimal cold storages of post-harvest fruits are necessary to enhance preservation, improve energy efficiency, reduce manual monitoring and improve food security along with quality especially in agricultural economies like Pakistan. An experiment using object detection and adaptive temperature control is uniquely performed in a humid subtropical climate. A YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm detects categories of fruit to adaptively control the set-point temperature of a cold storage refrigeration system. The algorithm differentiates fresh/stale bananas and apples to control compressor power of a 0.1-ton refrigerator. The object detecting system is 92 % accurate in sensing correct fruit. Adaptive temperature control through the compressor saves 30 % energy for bananas and 12 % for apples compared to conventional systems whilst passively regulating humidity and extending shelf-life of the fruit by 50 %. The methodology of this pilot-study can be extended to different foods beneficial for agriculture and transport sectors.

title: Bioinspired Cicada Wing Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Human Motion Monitoring and Mechanical Energy Harvesting
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of portable electronic devices has created an increasingly urgent demand for flexible and portable power sources. The triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) represents a promising technology for micro-energy harvesting, capable of efficiently converting mechanical energy from the environment into electricity. However, its output performance as a local power source is limited by insufficient contact efficiency and low charge density at triboelectric interfaces. Inspired by the nanocone array structure found on cicada wings, this study proposes a synergistic enhancement strategy that combines bioinspired cicada wing microstructures with corona discharge treatment, leading to the development of a high-performance bioinspired cicada wing TENG (BCW-TENG). Using lithography and template replication processes, micro-nano structures were fabricated on the PDMS surface, significantly increasing the effective contact area of the device and raising the open-circuit voltage by approximately 131% compared to a flat reference device. With further surface charge injection via corona discharge, the output performance was enhanced by another ∼165%, achieving an open-circuit voltage of 70 V and a peak power density of 57.38 mW/m2. By optimizing the power management circuit, the single-cycle energy storage efficiency was improved by a factor of 81. When employed as a se…

title: Description of charged-particle multiplicity distributions in high-energy proton–proton collisions based on a two-component model and examination of parton distribution functions
abstract: High-energy proton–proton collisions provide an important probe of small-x gluon dynamics in quantum chromodynamics. In this work, charged-particle pseudorapidity distributions in high-energy pp collisions are studied within a two-component model. The central component is described by gluon–gluon fusion using unintegrated gluon distributions constructed with the Kimber–Martin–Ryskin prescription, while the fragmentation component is modeled through quark recombination with collinear parton distributions. The integrated PDFs are evolved using the modified DGLAP equations including nonlinear gluon-recombination corrections. The calculated [Formula: see text] distributions are compared with ATLAS data at [Formula: see text], [Formula: see text], [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text]. After normalization at midrapidity, the model reproduces the main features of the measured distributions, with gluon fusion dominating the central rapidity region. Comparisons with CT18, MSHT20, NNPDF, HERAPDF2.0 and GRV98 PDFs show that the pseudorapidity shape is sensitive to the small-x behavior of the gluon distribution. The results suggest that charged-particle pseudorapidity distributions can serve as a useful phenomenological test of small-x gluon PDFs within two-component models.

title: Integration of Virtual Lab-Based Learning Media in Improving Practical Skills and Student Engagement in Computer Network Engineering
abstract: This study investigates the integration of learning media using virtual labs to improve practical skills and student engagement in Computer Network Engineering at Institut Teknologi dan Bisnis Bina Sarana Global. A quasi-experimental design was conducted in an experimental class using virtual labs and in a control class using the traditional practicum. Participants consisted of 62 students. Data were collected with pretest–posttest assessments of practicum skills and an evidence-rated engagement questionnaire. The results showed a great increase in the experimental class. Then, using a series of independent-samples t-tests, we compared the posttest practical skill scores between the experimental (M = 85.42, SD = 6.31) and control class practice (M = 78.11, SD = 7.04), t(60) = 4.21, p < .001, and a large effect size (d = 1.06). In addition, a comparison of the groups' mean scored on short-answer scoring revealed that students were more engaged with the material in the experimental group (M = 4.32, SD = 0.41) than compared to students in the control group (M = 3.87, SD = 0.46), t(60) = -3.78, p < .001. In general, they are effective in providing laboratory practice to master concepts, demonstrate bad practices, troubleshoot, and in encouraging active participation in learning. title: Complementary Hydrogel-Based Ionic Thermoelectric Systems for Photovoltaic Waste Heat Harvesting and Energy Storage
abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) operation generates substantial low-grade waste heat, motivating energy-recovery strategies that can accommodate dynamically varying thermal conditions. Here, thermogalvanic and thermodiffusive hydrogel-based ionic thermoelectric (iTE) devices were separately integrated with the same PV-phase change composite (PCC) platform to compare their energy-conversion and energy-delivery characteristics. The PAM-F thermogalvanic cell (TC) exhibited an ionic Seebeck coefficient of 1.37 mV K–1 and a maximum power density of 4.16 mW m–2 at ΔT = 10 K, while maintaining electrical output under an external load for over 1 h. In contrast, the thermodiffusive PVA-K iTE supercapacitor exhibited a larger negative ionic Seebeck coefficient of –4.28 mV K–1 and enabled thermal charging followed by time-shifted electrical discharge. The PCC suppressed the cold-side temperature rise during irradiation and maintained a larger temperature gradient across the iTE layer, while releasing stored latent heat after irradiation to reverse the thermal gradient. Under simulated PV operation, the PVA-K-based system generated –36.8 mV at a temperature difference of approximately 11 K and subsequently developed a reversed open-circuit voltage of 21.4 mV, delivering 12.65 mJ m–2 of electrical energy during post-irradiation discharge. These results reveal two complementary modes for PV waste…

title: Multi-omics integration identifies COQ8A in excitatory neurons as a protective gene in major depressive disorder
Two-stage stochastic optimization for planning and operation of multiple types of mobile energy resources in distribution networks
abstract: High penetrations of wind and photovoltaic (PV) generation increase temporal and scenario-dependent source–load variability in distribution networks, complicating the planning and operation of mobile energy resources. This paper proposes a multi-scenario-driven planning–operation co-optimization method that incorporates mobile energy storage vehicles (MESVs), transportable battery energy storage systems (TBESSs), mobile hydrogen fuel-cell power supply vehicles (MHSVs), power-to-hydrogen (P2H), and on-site hydrogen storage into a two-stage stochastic optimization framework. Probability-weighted representative scenarios characterize wind, photovoltaic, and load uncertainty. The first stage determines resource types, quantities, ratings, candidate-node activation, and P2H/hydrogen-storage capacities; the second stage determines scenario-dependent deployment and hourly operation. A second-order cone-relaxed DistFlow model represents battery operation, the P2H–storage–refueling–MHSV chain, road accessibility, and relocation costs. Representative cases for renewable energy integration, peak shaving, congestion mitigation, and black-start active-power support are tested on the IEEE 33-bus system. In the renewable-integration case, three TBESSs totaling 4.50 MW/11.25 MWh reduce monthly wind/PV curtailment from 571.908 to 461.385 MWh, a 19.3% reduction. In the peak-shaving case, road co…

title: Exploring AI Integration in South Korean K-12 Education: Teachers’ Practices, Motivations, and Ethical Considerations
abstract: Despite growing interest in Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted language learning, little is known about how K–12 teachers in South Korea navigate this integration. This qualitative case study explores how K–12 English teachers in South Korea are integrating AI into their educational practices, aiming to understand their experiences with innovative teaching approaches, as well as the challenges and ethical concerns they encounter. Data were collected from seven AI-engaged English teachers across elementary, middle, and high schools through teaching logs, learning artifacts, and focus group interviews. The findings reveal that AI reduced time spent on administrative tasks, freeing time for lesson planning. Also, teachers reported increased learner agency among students, more diversified learning modalities, and lowered participation barriers in learning activities. However, most teachers were unaware of the ethical considerations of AI and current AI guidelines were unsupportive. This study provides firsthand qualitative evidence of how K–12 English teachers in South Korea integrate AI into their everyday practice, while revealing a critical gap between official policy dissemination and teachers' actual awareness of guidelines for effective and responsible AI use.

title: A stable semi-implicit two-step GFDM for the k –ω turbulence model: Positivity, boundedness, and energy stability on non-uniform grids
abstract: A modification in explicit, unconditionally stable scheme is proposed for solving time-dependent partial differential equations. In contrast to the conventional DuFort–Frankel method, the proposed scheme allows sufficient positivity conditions to be identified for the resulting numerical solution. The proposed scheme is first-order accurate in time, while its spatial accuracy depends on the order of the Generalized Finite Difference Method (GFDM). Fourier series analysis is provided for proving the scheme to be unconditionally stable. The plots for stability regions of the scheme are also provided. The convergence of the scheme is also provided for system of convection diffusion equations. The scheme is applied for solving k–[Formula: see text] turbulent model of non-Newtonian fluid flow over Riga plate with heat and mass transfer. An energy estimate of the proposed scheme for nonlinear model of Turbulent flow under the effects of heat and mass transfer on a non-uniform grid is also established. A non-uniform grid is constructed for considered turbulent boundary layer flow in which fine grid is used near the wall/plate and course grid is used away from the plate. Furthermore, positivity and boundedness of proposed scheme are established for Stokes’ first problem on the non-uniform grid. The comparison of proposed scheme is made with existing Euler and DuFort Frankel methods, an…

X-muscle actuator with selective regional contraction for a biohybrid rotatable joint
abstract: Abstract Biohybrid robots that utilize selective regional contraction of skeletal muscle have potential for achieving diverse movements, yet they face challenges such as insufficient spatial utilization and integration. In this study, an X-muscle actuator (XMA) was developed to address these issues. Using skeletal muscle cells, the XMA was designed with regional response characteristics and uniform contraction capability. The performance of the XMA was characterized, with maximum active contractile force reaching 2.97 mN. A biohybrid rotatable joint, integrating the XMA with mechanical structures, achieved a maximum unidirectional rotation angle of 1.39° under electrical stimulation, and multi-directional movements were realized through composite stimulation. This work not only enhances the movement diversity of biohybrid robots but also establishes a new paradigm for combining intrinsic biological tissue properties with advanced mechanical design, laying the foundation for the next generation of higher-performance, more versatile biohybrid systems.

The IDEA Design Scaffold: A Developmental Framework for Functional Ideation in Systemic Design
abstract: Abstract Functional ideation in systemic design unfolds within sociotechnical and sociocultural environments where goals, constraints, and evaluative criteria evolve across multiple levels of organization. Creativity research explains important aspects of novelty, variation, recombination, and selective retention, but it often treats novelty as emerging within a relatively stable representational space or a single level of abstraction. Systemic design scholarship, in turn, has developed strong approaches for framing complexity, mapping relations, organizing participation, and coordinating action, but it less often specifies how designers navigate between systemic levels, address challenges at different levels of abstraction, and construct intervention candidates while the task environment is still being differentiated. This paper responds by proposing a naturalistic framework of ideation within the Interactivist–Constructivist paradigm, with the IDEA Design Scaffold as its methodological architecture for systemic design. The central claim is that functional ideation under systemic complexity must be understood as a self-directed developmental process: intervention opportunities become novel and appropriate as designers navigate across levels of complexity through anticipatory exploration, partial stabilization, reflective reorganization, and rebuilding of missing supports. title: Boosting playful work design: a test of a micro and modular e-intervention
abstract: Purpose Playful work design (PWD) refers to approaching and performing work activities playfully to foster fun and challenge. In this study, we build on the idea that PWD stems from a malleable metacognitive competency that can be cultivated through intentional activities. Design/methodology/approach Accordingly, we developed and tested a micro (Study 1) and a modular PWD e-intervention (Study 2) aimed at nurturing the knowledge, skills and abilities central to PWD. Findings Results of Study 1 (N = 74 individuals, n = 432 days) revealed that actively completing exercises can promote designing competition but not designing fun. In Study 2, individuals who actively participated in the modular e-intervention increased in both designing fun and designing competition (N = 127 individuals; n = 549 weeks). In both studies, mere exposure to the e-intervention did not predict outcomes. Across both studies, PWD was positively related to creative performance through informal learning (Study 1) and self-efficacy (Study 2). Originality/value The findings highlight the promise of e-interventions in cultivating PWD, which can help to strengthen employees' creative performance.

title: Design of Iron-Based Fischer–Tropsch Synthesis Catalysts for Directly Converting Syngas to Value-Added Chemicals and Clean Fuels
abstract: Conspectus Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS) represents a key technology for converting syngas into fuels and value-added chemicals. Despite decades of industrial application, it remains constrained by three persistent challenges: the dynamic reconstruction of active phases under working conditions, broad hydrocarbon distributions arising from complex reaction pathways, and substantial CO2 formation via the water–gas shift (WGS) side reaction. To address these challenges, our group has made continuous efforts through three stages in the last dozen years: establishing the relationship between active-phase dynamics and catalytic performance, regulating product distribution through electronic modulation and dual-site coupling, and suppressing WGS activity by engineering hydrophobic microenvironments. Relating active-phase dynamics to catalytic performance requires resolving the formation and transformation of Fe phases during FTS. Iron oxide precursors undergo reduction and carburization to form iron carbides, which serve as key active phases for CO activation, C–C coupling, and hydrocarbon formation. Analysis of the reduction and carburization pathways of Fe species, together with the evolution of surface carbon species, allowed us to correlate bulk and surface Fe-phase compositions with catalytic performance. title: Turning distress into distraction: using virtual reality during penicillin injections for rheumatic fever
abstract: aim: In Aotearoa New Zealand, people with acute rheumatic fever (ARF) receive 4-weekly intramuscular benzathine penicillin G (BPG) injections for a minimum of 10 years to prevent recurrence and progression to rheumatic heart disease. Within a phase IIA trial of a higher-dose subcutaneous injection of penicillin (SCIP), which provides at least 10 weeks of coverage, we piloted immersive virtual reality (VR) distraction to assess whether it improved injection acceptability through reductions in pain and anxiety. methods: Ten participants aged 9–20 years used a Meta Quest VR headset during their SCIP procedure. Participants rated anxiety before and after the injection and reported both their usual injection pain (based on prior SCIP injections) and pain during the current injection using zero to 10 scales. Acceptability and user experience were assessed through structured feedback from participants, caregivers and nurses. results: Acceptability of the VR headset was high; all participants reported they would use VR again and recommend it to others. Mean pain scores decreased from 5.1 (usual) to 3.3 (current), and mean anxiety from 3.4 (pre-injection) to 1.1 (postinjection). Impact of virtual and hands-on laboratory experimentation on the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge: a meta-analysis
abstract: Introduction Hands-on laboratory experimentation is an important contributor to the successful acquisition of conceptual science knowledge, but its practical application has several limitations. Virtual laboratory experiments help overcome most of these shortcomings and may also be more effective than hands-on laboratory activities in promoting conceptual science knowledge acquisition. Methods In this study, the impact of virtual and hands-on laboratory experimentation on the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge was compared by means of a meta-analysis. The meta-analysis encompassed 43 studies selected according to the predefined inclusion criteria, and the principles of Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses procedure. For each study, one effect size value of Hedges' g was calculated. Subsequently, due to their heterogeneity, the overall effect size value was computed through the use of the random-effects model. Results Based on the obtained results [ g = 0.551, SE = 0.097, 95% CI (0.362, 0.740), p < 0.001] virtual laboratory experimentation appears to be significantly more effective in promoting the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge than experimentation conducted in hands-on laboratories. title: Exogenous plant growth regulators alleviate natural high temperature stress after anthesis in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) by sustaining efficient photosynthesis and antioxidant defense responses
abstract: Introduction High temperature stress during the grain-filling period severely suppresses plant growth and yield formation in winter wheat. Plant growth regulators including 2,4-epibrassinolide (EBR) and melatonin (MT) have been reported to effectively enhance plant thermotolerance, representing a promising strategy to mitigate extreme high temperature stress and stabilize wheat yield. Methods In this study, integrated agronomic, physiological and transcriptomic analyses were conducted to explore the regulatory effects of different exogenous plant growth regulators on thermotolerance and physiological characteristics of winter wheat during the grain-filling stage. Results and discussion Exogenous application of these regulators modulated the expression of core photosynthesis-related genes, increased the net photosynthetic rate of flag leaves, enhanced photosynthetic capacity, and alleviated heat-induced damage. Meanwhile, exogenous regulators altered the transcript levels of key antioxidant enzyme-coding genes, thereby boosting antioxidant enzyme activities, reducing the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA), and relieving membrane lipid peroxidation. title: Non-target-site resistance mechanisms to glyphosate in Eleusine indica from Xinjiang cotton fields
abstract: Glyphosate resistance in weeds is often mediated by target-site changes in 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase (EPSPS), but non-target-site resistance (NTSR) mechanisms are increasingly recognized as important contributors to field-evolved resistance. Here, we characterized a glyphosate-resistant Eleusine indica population collected from cotton fields in Xinjiang, China. Whole-plant dose–response analysis showed that the resistant population GR-R had a 3.36-fold higher GR 50 than the susceptible population GR-S. GR-R also accumulated substantially less shikimic acid after glyphosate treatment (approximately two-fold lower than GR-S at 24 and 48 hours after treatment), indicating reduced impact on the shikimate pathway. However, sequencing of a conserved EPSPS region revealed no substitutions at known resistance-associated residues, and EPSPS expression did not differ significantly between GR-R and GR-S. RNA-seq analysis identified 364 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment of oxidative stress, carbohydrate metabolism, amino acid metabolism, hormone signaling, and transporter-related processes. Four upregulated genes associated with herbicide metabolic resistance, CYP94C1 , ABCA7 , ABCG37 , and ABCG39 , were validated by qPCR. Structural modeling and molecular docking suggested potential interactions between glyphosate and the encoded proteins, with ABCG39 showi…

title: African Medicinal Plant Extracts in Diabetes Mellitus: Integrating Preclinical Evidence, Clinical Studies, and Translational Perspectives
abstract: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity is associated with metabolic dysfunction, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and progressive injury to metabolically active organs including the liver and kidneys. Cucumeropsis mannii is an underutilised oilseed rich in bioactive phytochemicals with reported antioxidant and hypolipidaemic properties. This study investigated the protective effects of dietary C. mannii supplementation against HFD-induced metabolic, biochemical and histopathological alterations in pubertal male Wistar rats. Sixty-four pubertal male Wistar rats were randomly assigned into eight groups (n = 8/group) receiving standard diet, HFD, C. mannii (5%, 10%, or 20%) incorporated into standard diet, or HFD supplemented with corresponding concentrations of C. mannii for four weeks. Body weight and feed intake were monitored throughout the study. Serum glucose, insulin, adiponectin, leptin, amylase and lipase were assayed, while hepatic and renal oxidative stress markers (total antioxidant capacity and malondialdehyde) and inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-10) were determined. Liver and kidney tissues were evaluated histologically using haematoxylin and eosin and periodic acid-Schiff staining. Engineering plant tandem kinase immune receptors expands effector recognition profiles
abstract: Plant intracellular immune receptors are widely deployed in breeding to protect crops from disease. In addition to nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat receptors (NLRs), tandem kinase proteins (TKPs) have recently emerged as an important family of immune receptors within staple cereal food crops, but how TKPs recognize effectors and whether they are amenable to engineering is essentially unknown. Here, we show that the barley and wheat TKPs Rmo2 and Rwt7 recognize different blast fungus effectors via their integrated HMA domains using different protein interfaces with nanomolar binding affinity. Structural analysis pinpointed interface residues that dictate effector recognition and enabled engineering of dual-specificity TKPs. These results establish integrated HMA domains as programmable modules within TKPs for designing new specificities in plant immunity for diseases relevant to global agriculture.

title: Novel juxtamembrane FLT3 in-frame insertion in a child with refractory AML: a case report of durable remission following allogeneic HSCT and FLT3 inhibitor therapy
abstract: Background FLT3 gene mutations, particularly internal tandem duplications ( FLT3 -ITD), are present in approximately 25%–30% of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and are important drivers of leukemogenesis; less frequently, FLT3 mutations occur as tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) variants. Non-canonical variants, such as juxtamembrane domain (JMD) in-frame insertions, are rare and their pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic sensitivities are less defined. Case description We report a 13-year-old female patient with refractory AML harboring a novel in-frame insertion in the FLT3 JMD NC_000013.11(NM_004119.3):c.1780_1781insGGGTCCCTCCGCCTACCC; p.(Phe594delinsTrpValProProProThrLeu) identified by next-generation sequencing (NGS). The disease was resistant to standard intensive chemotherapy but showed marked sensitivity to the FLT3 inhibitor sorafenib. Following relapse upon sorafenib discontinuation due to cardiac toxicity, the patient underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) while in active disease (M3 marrow). A sequential myeloablative conditioning regimen consisting of melphalan, fludarabine, and fractionated total body irradiation (TBI-8 Gray) was employed. Post-transplant, sorafenib maintenance was resumed for 2 years. Outcomes The patient achieved sustained complete remission and remains disease-free 63 months post-HSCT, despite significant pre…

An efficiency-oriented hierarchical energy management strategy for renewable electric-hydrogen systems with adaptive multi-stack PEMFC activation
abstract: Abstract The growing integration of renewable energy sources requires efficient management strategies for electric-hydrogen coupled systems. Conventional single fuel cell configurations suffer from limited power capacity and poor efficiency under dynamic conditions, while existing power allocation methods for multi-stack fuel cell systems often neglect the coordinated effects of battery state of charge and hydrogen storage conditions. This study proposes a hierarchical energy management strategy for electric-hydrogen coupled multi-stack proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) systems, combining a supervisory state-machine layer with an equipment-level control layer. The upper layer determines the optimal operating state by considering residual power demand, lithium battery state of charge, and hydrogen storage state, and dynamically allocates the number of active fuel cell stacks. The lower layer implements the corresponding commands through individual device controllers to coordinate photovoltaic generation, energy storage, hydrogen production, and fuel cell operation. By keeping PEMFC operation near its high-efficiency region, the strategy reduces unnecessary stack activation and improves stability under variable operating conditions. MATLAB/Simulink simulations show that the proposed strategy achieves smoother power transitions, higher fuel cell efficiency, and stable ope…

title: Long term operation of dual chamber microbial fuel cells for energy production and monitoring physicochemical changes of landfill leachate treatment
abstract: Abstract The present study investigates the efficiency of dual-chamber microbial fuel cells (DC-MFCs) in treating municipal landfill leachate at different concentrations (100%, 75%, 50% and 25%) during a 60-day batch operation. A DC-MFC with an anode volume of 1300 ml and a cathode of 650 ml, carbon cloth electrodes (8.5 cm diameter), and Nafion 117 membrane was analyzed with respect to physicochemical changes, energy recovery, and coulombic efficiency (CE). To accelerate the formation of the biofilm layer, the same initial leachate sample was grown in BHI culture medium and added to each MFC at a rate of 10% by volume. Key parameters, including pH, electrical conductivity (EC), alkalinity, chloride concentration, and chemical oxygen demand (COD), were monitored along with energy production through polarization curves. Blank samples were used as controls to confirm treatment efficacy. Results showed that the maximum COD removal efficiency was observed in reactors with concentrations of 100%, 75%, 50%, and 25%, achieving efficiencies of 99.32%, 99.28%, 98.75%, and 98.38%, respectively. The trends of EC, alkalinity, and chloride ion changes were similar and decreasing, while pH increased at all concentrations. title: Risky social media challenges: Young adults’ exposure, participation, and evaluations
abstract: Abstract Risky social media challenges (i.e., videos of people recording high-risk behaviors while encouraging others to do the same) are popular. This study explored young people’s exposure to, engagement in, and evaluations of, these challenges. Findings of a survey among adolescents and young adults ( N = 386; aged 16–25) revealed frequent exposure to these challenges (88.1 %), mostly carried out by unknown individuals (71.2 %) and through Instagram (61.1 %) and TikTok (58.0 %). Having participated in a challenge themselves was reported by 34.7 % of the participants, with only 10.4 % posting about it online, and 12.7 % trying to persuade others to also participate. Moreover, relatively negative evaluations (attitudes, social injunctive and descriptive norms, and behavioral intentions) of risky social media challenges were found. Taken together, the results show a discrepancy between youth evaluations of, and their actual engagements in, risky social media challenges. More research on this discrepancy is needed and prevention or regulation of this rising phenomenon with potentially harmful consequences is warranted.

title: Third-generation ultralong-term latent heat storage glass based on a sugar alcohol mixture
abstract: Long-term thermal storage can decarbonize heat utilization by resolving mismatches between heat supply and demand. However, common heat storage materials cannot store energy for long periods. Here, we report an ultralong-term latent heat storage “glass” based on a ternary eutectic sugar alcohol mixture. The as-prepared material exhibits a solid–liquid phase change and glass transition at 423 and 289 K, respectively, with heat release via cold crystallization at 346 K. Remarkably, the glass transition temperature increases to 313 K after aging at ambient temperature for 12 hours due to structural relaxation. This phase change material (PCM) conserves the latent heat of fusion at 423 K for at least 180 days in the glass state at ambient temperature. These results establish a third-generation latent heat storage mode, retaining the charged state as a kinetically arrested amorphous solid and thereby fundamentally shifting the stability criterion from supercooled-liquid nucleation suppression to glass-transition and structural-relaxation kinetics.

title: Grain size and sediment storage explain why postfire debris flows are absent in some mountainous landscapes
abstract: Postfire debris flow occurrence varies widely in mountainous landscapes, even under similar rainfall conditions. To understand why, we investigated two burned landscapes that experienced intense postfire rainfall: one in southern California with over 100 postfire debris flows and one in northern California with no postfire debris flows. Debris flows can initiate from bed failures that are predicted to occur when Shields stress τ ∗ exceeds a threshold. We characterized τ ∗ at the two sites, investigated bed failure, and conducted numerical experiments to identify controlling factors. Postfire increases in clear-water runoff raised τ ∗ by up to threefold, whereas postfire reductions in channel grain size raised τ ∗ by two orders of magnitude. No increase in runoff was required to initiate debris flows at the southern California site, yet debris flows were unlikely to initiate at the northern California site even for considerable increases in runoff. These results provide a mechanistic explanation for discrepancies in debris flow occurrence in mountainous landscapes.

title: From social learning mechanisms to cultural participation: the mediating role of learning culture in Miao embroidery communities
abstract: Research into the sustainability of traditional crafts has focused on preservation, digitalization, design innovation, and creative economy; however, there has been relatively little emphasis on the micro-level dynamics through which community learning leads to sustainable Participation in culture. This study examines the relationships between social learning processes, learning culture, cultural Participation, and cultural outcomes in Miao embroidery communities in Guizhou, China. Social learning is defined by three mechanisms: community interaction, observational learning, and Participation in practice. In a quantitative cross-sectional research design, data were gathered from 280 purposively sampled Miao embroiderers and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings show that community interaction, observational learning, and Participation in practice are positively related to learning culture, which in turn is positively related to cultural Participation. Cultural Participation is the strongest predictor of attachment to cultural identity, including embroidery practice and Participation in cultural events. Assessing regional wind behavior and resource potential using MERRA-2 reanalysis data and experimentally measured mast data
abstract: Abstract The main objective of this research is to assess the wind energy potential of the Manaydara region in South Sikkim, India, by collecting real-time wind resource data through a practically installed Weather Monitoring System (WMS). For comparative analysis and validation, on-site ground-based wind measurements were evaluated alongside reanalysis data obtained from the NASA MERRA-2 assimilation product, using data corresponding to the same location and measurement height. The MERRA-2 dataset was selected over the MERRA and IMDAA datasets for wind resource assessment because of its improved data quality, broader spatial coverage, greater accuracy, and enhanced compatibility with modern analytical tools. In the initial phase of analysis, 15- minute step data is collected at 10- meters height is being preprocessed, extrapolated to 50- meters level, and averaged over diurnal, monthly, seasonal, and annual time frames. To model the wind resources stochastically, a descriptive statistical analysis is being performed at micro level, followed by distributing fitting analysis using Weibull distribution function. Furthermore, directional wind rose and associated wind power densities are computed. title: Segment-Resolved Intramolecular Dual Z-Scheme-Like Electron Transfer Driven by Built-in Electric Field in a Monomeric Photocatalyst for Efficient Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
abstract: Abstract Research on built-in electric fields (BIEFs) is typically focused on the interfaces of heterojunctions or the overall behavior of polymeric materials, which often neglects the local electronic interactions within the subcomponents. Here, we propose that a single–component photocatalyst can be regarded as a generalized heterojunction by dividing it into multiple spatially independent segments with different electronic properties. We prepared a conjugated polymer (CN-K/SC) with significant intramolecular charge inhomogeneity by functionalizing sulfonyl cyanide (SC) groups onto carbon nitride (CN) using the facile KSCN molten salt method. This inhomogeneity generates a strong BIEF that drives directional migration of photogenerated carriers. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM), In situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (In situ XPS), and theoretical calculations collectively reveal the complex dynamics of photogenerated carriers. CN-K/SC was divided into three spatially adjacent regions with comparable excitation energies through excited-state calculations and spatial charge distribution analysis. Under the BIEF, these regions interact synergistically to establish a dual Z-scheme-like electron transfer pathway. This pathway enhances charge separation efficiency and boosts the photocatalytic H2O2 production (PHP) rate (approximately 28 times that of the pristine CN). This …

title: Development and external validation of a nomogram to predict survival and guide surgical strategy for colorectal cancer with synchronous liver and lung metastases: a SEER-based analysis
abstract: Surgical management of colorectal cancer with synchronous liver and lung metastases (CRC-SLLM) remains challenging because of marked clinical heterogeneity, and reliable tools for individualized risk assessment are lacking. We aimed to develop and externally validate a nomogram for overall survival (OS) prediction and to explore its potential value in guiding selection for primary tumor resection (PTR). Patients diagnosed with CRC-SLLM between 2010 and 2015 were identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database and randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 808) and an internal validation cohort (n = 345) in a 7:3 ratio, whereas external validation was performed using 65 patients from the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University, China. After feature selection with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, a multivariable Cox-based nomogram was constructed, and its performance was assessed using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, decision curve analysis (DCA), and risk stratification. The final nomogram incorporated nine predictors: age, primary tumor site, histological grade, tumor size, N stage, bone metastasis, carcinoembryonic antigen status, metastasectomy, and chemotherapy. It showed stable discrimination across the training, internal validation, and external validation co…

abstract: Abstract STUDY QUESTION Is the number of MII (metaphase II) oocytes comparable in the two-shot protocol versus the conventional corifollitropin alfa (CFA) followed by follitropin-beta protocol? SUMMARY ANSWER Although the mean number of MII oocytes did not differ significantly between the two-shot protocol and the control group, non-inferiority was not statistically met. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY Controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) protocols are often associated with significant side effects, largely due to the burden of multiple daily injections. Efforts to develop more patient-friendly protocols include the shift from GnRH-agonist to antagonist protocols and the introduction of progestin protocol for pituitary suppression (PPS). While such patient-friendly approaches benefit infertile patients, they are even more appealing for women undergoing COS for elective fertility preservation. The current study aims to compare a novel ovarian stimulation protocol involving two sequential CFA injections (two-shot protocol) with a conventional approach using CFA and follitropin-beta in elective fertility preservation. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION Phase III, randomized, controlled, single-center, non-inferiority clinical trial conducted at a Fertility Unit within a University-Affiliated Hospital between December 2023 and July 2025. Consumer acceptance of cultivated meat: a systematic review and integrated perception-to-strategy framework
abstract: Purpose This study synthesises research on consumer acceptance of cultivated meat (CM) and develops a framework explaining how contextual conditions shape the interpretation of product, market and legitimation cues, how inhibiting and enabling evaluations perform distinct functions, and how these processes relate to differentiated adoption outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A multi-method systematic review of 42 peer-reviewed empirical articles followed PRISMA guidelines. An antecedents-decisions-outcomes (ADO) synthesis mapped study-level relationships, while structural topic modelling (STM) identified corpus-level thematic structure and temporal development. Findings The synthesis shows that CM acceptance is not adequately explained as an additive balance of barriers and drivers. External cues acquire meaning through context-dependent evaluations, while inhibiting and enabling evaluations perform distinct, non-equivalent functions. STM confirmed persistent psychological inhibitors and revealed increasing attention to sensory, packaging, organisational, symbolic and willingness-to-pay themes. The resulting integrated perception-to-strategy (IPS) framework links contextual conditions and cue interpretation to asymmetric inhibiting-enabling processes and three analytically distinct outcomes: initial receptivity, market commitment and sustained adoption. title: Association of a routine dexmedetomidine-remifentanil anesthetic strategy with POD3 morning cortisol change in older patients undergoing radical esophagectomy
abstract: Background Older patients undergoing radical esophagectomy may experience marked postoperative endocrine stress, inflammation, pain, and short-term cognitive decline. We evaluated whether a routine anesthetic strategy combining dexmedetomidine with remifentanil was associated with a smaller POD3 serum cortisol increase than remifentanil- or dexmedetomidine-based strategies alone. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort screened 426 consecutive patients aged ≥65 years who underwent elective radical esophagectomy from January 2023 to December 2025. Of these, 347 had verifiable pathway-based POD3 biomarker and POD7 MoCA data after predefined clinical, laboratory, and follow-up exclusions. The primary analysis used a prespecified balanced common-support analytic cohort drawn from the naturally occurring REM (continuous remifentanil without dexmedetomidine), DEX (dexmedetomidine with non-remifentanil opioid analgesia and without continuous remifentanil), and Dex-REM (both infusions) exposure strata (100 patients each). The primary endpoint was morning serum cortisol change from preoperative day 1 to postoperative day 3 (POD3). Results POD7 screening-based cognitive decline occurred in 51 patients in the balanced common-support cohort. abstract: On the ancient bronze artifacts unearthed in Weifang, there are a large number of decorative patterns with distinct local styles, which are important visual records of local craft traditions. In the face of the outstanding problems exposed in the actual inheritance of such traditional skills at present-such as the scattered distribution of bronze pattern data, the difficulty of systematic access, the excessive emphasis on digital collection in the research work and the neglect of the production process and skill core, and the difficulty of the existing digital resources to truly transform into productivity that can be used for creative design, this study starts from the basic position of digital empowerment and transformation and innovation, combined with a number of practical application projects, and systematically sorts out the specific operation processes of a series of technical links such as three-dimensional scanning, photographic measurement, pattern vector reconstruction, immersive interactive experience, and cultural and creative development based on digital printing. On this basis, a three-layer progressive application path of “collection-communication-transformation” is built. title: Rapport-building dialogue strategy: a comprehensive analysis of human subjective, behavioral and facial emotional engagement
abstract: Purpose Rapport is a conversational aspect focused on relationship building. Because rapport can influence outcomes in collaborative tasks, this study proposes a concrete methodology for introducing rapport-building into dialogue systems, namely a rapport-building dialogue strategy, and evaluates its effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach We implemented a rapport-building dialogue strategy for virtual agents by prompting a large language model (LLM) based on psychological theories of rapport. We employed two dialogue approaches, a predefined sequence and a free-form approach, to guide dialogue generation and compared their performance through human evaluations. To analyze the human aspects of rapport further, we conducted subjective, behavioral and facial emotion assessments. Findings Our experimental results show that the system based on a free-form dialogue strategy, which allows the adaptive use of rapport-building strategies, achieves the highest subjective scores. Our human-centered analyses reveal strong associations between rapport perception and user experience, indicating that perceived rapport is closely aligned with engagement and experiential quality. We observe directional tendencies in behavioral and emotional patterns, with more expressive participants tending to report higher rapport scores, suggesting potential associations that warrant further investigatio…

Optimizing Intraocular Lens Power Calculations in Eyes with Short Axial Length
abstract: This review evaluates the challenges of intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation in eyes with short axial length (AL) and examines the impact of modern optical biometry and new generation of artificial intelligence (AI) based formulas on refractive outcomes. Short AL eyes remain challenging for accurate IOL power calculation and are consistently associated with increased prediction error and refractive surprises. This is largely due to the disproportionate effect of minor biometric errors and difficulties in estimating effective lens position in small eyes. The introduction of advanced optical biometers, such as IOLMaster 700, has significantly improved measurement precision by enhancing the accuracy of AL and anterior chamber depth assessments. Furthermore, AI-based IOL formulas, such as Kane and Prediction Enhanced by Artificial Intelligence and output Linearisation – Debellemaniére, Gatinel, Saad (Pearl-DGS), which utilize large datasets and non-linear machine learning models, have demonstrated superior refractive predictability compared to traditional formulas such as Hoffer Q and Sanders-Retzlaff-Kraff/Theoretical (SRK/T). Cooke K6 formula (K6) which incorporated prediction modification, has shown the highest prediction accuracy. title: Gendered Power: Emma Hale Smith in Nauvoo, 1842-1844
abstract: This paper investigates how gendered power operates within a religious community. It utilizes a close historical study of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Nauvoo, Illinois between 1842 and 1844. It asserts that institutional authority given to the prophet’s wife, Emma Smith, expanded and contracted in response to her individual assertions of power. These expressions of power primarily involve Joseph Smith’s practice of polygamy, which Emma generally did not agree with. This paper relies on recently published archives from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

title: The impact of formal power and informal power on firm innovation: the asymmetric moderating roles of digital transformation
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine the influence of formal power and informal power on firm innovation, with a particular focus on the moderating role of digital transformation. Design/methodology/approach The research sample consisted of Chinese A-share manufacturing firms between 2007 and 2024. Findings The research results indicate that both formal power and informal power have a significantly positive impact on firm innovation. However, the moderating effect of digital transformation on the impact of formal power and informal power is asymmetrical. In particular, digital transformation exerts a negative moderating effect on the relationship between formal power and firm innovation, whereas it exerts a positive moderating effect on the relationship between informal power and firm innovation. These results are subsequently validated through a series of robustness tests. Originality/value Firstly, this paper unpacks CEO power to examine the impact of formal power and informal power on firm innovation, rather than regarding it as an aggregate construct. Secondly, this paper contributes to the literature on digital transformation by empirically examining how digital transformation changes the impact of formal power and informal power on firm innovation. title: Online retail experience as a driver of brand stereotypes and psychological brand ownership
abstract: Purpose Experiential marketing has gained significant traction in today’s economy due to the value consumers place on favorable, memorable experiences with a brand and its platforms. Accordingly, this research aims to investigate how the online retail experience (ORE) affects the stereotyping of the brands in question and consumers’ psychological inclination to own them. The authors study a model of the relationships among ORE, brand stereotypes (i.e. brand warmth and brand competence) and psychological brand ownership (PBO). Design/methodology/approach The authors collected 408 valid responses via self-administered online surveys. The analysis was performed through structural equation modeling in AMOS v.27. Findings The results demonstrate that ORE affects brand warmth, brand competence and PBO. Brand warmth also emerged as a predictor of PBO. Further, the moderating effect of perceived brand ethicality was established. Practical implications Marketers should focus on delivering a memorable, glitch-free ORE to foster favorable brand perceptions and a sense of PBO among platform users. Originality/value This research advances the literature by applying the stereotype content model and psychological ownership theory in the online retail context. title: Value-based pricing of brensocatib for frequently exacerbating non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis in China: a China-adapted, FEV1-inclusive time-dependent markov analysis
abstract: Objective To estimate a China-specific value-based annual price (P*) for brensocatib 25 mg added to standard care (SC), compared with SC alone, in adults with frequently exacerbating non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, and to assess how strongly the estimate depends on transferred assumptions linking forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV 1 ) to long-term outcomes. Methods A seven-state Markov cohort model with monthly cycles and a lifetime horizon was constructed from the Chinese healthcare system perspective. Chinese sources informed the target population, exacerbation burden, baseline microbiology, background mortality, resource use, costs, discounting, and decision context, while ASPEN supplied the exacerbation rate ratio (0.81) and annual FEV 1 decline (24 mL with brensocatib 25 mg vs. 62 mL with placebo). In the base case, cohort-mean FEV 1 was linked to utility and mortality through explicit external mappings. The primary willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was CNY 200,000 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY); uncertainty was examined with a paired 10,000-draw probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA). title: 儒家倫理視域下 iPSC 自動化系統人機關係的責任與信任建構
abstract: LANGUAGE NOTE | Document text in Chinese; abstract also in English. 高科技如誘導多能幹細胞（iPSC）的臨床轉化所依賴的自動化細胞培養、AI質控及手術輔助機器人，引發了責任歸屬模糊與信任的倫理難題，傳統以人為中心的倫理框架難以有效回應人機互動中的“黑箱决策”與責任彌散問題。本文從儒家“仁、義、禮、信”出發，提出關係性人機倫理分析框架：以“義”與“禮”明確開發者、操作者、監管者的分布式責任邊界；以“仁”與“信”論證信任不僅源於技術可靠性，更植根於人-機-機構關係中的誠意與仁心。進而提出“人技有義、人技有信”的倫理秩序，並從設計、應用、審查、監管四個層面給出實踐路徑。本文旨在為高技術醫療時代的人機關係提供植根於中華優秀傳統文化的倫理智慧，推動iPSC技術在“仁智合一”的軌道上健康發展。 The clinical application of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) increasingly depends on automated technologies, including robotic cell culture, artificial intelligence–assisted quality control, and surgical support systems. These technologies improve efficiency and precision, but they raise ethical concerns regarding the attribution of responsibility and the basis of trust in human–machine interaction. It argues that yi and li can help define the responsibilities of developers, operators, and regulators, while ren and xin suggest that trust depends not only on technical performance but also on sincerity and benevolence in human–machine–institutional relations. On this basis, the paper proposes an eth…

abstract_zh: LANGUAGE NOTE | Document text in Chinese; abstract also in English. 高科技如誘導多能幹細胞（iPSC）的臨床轉化所依賴的自動化細胞培養、AI質控及手術輔助機器人，引發了責任歸屬模糊與信任的倫理難題，傳統以人為中心的倫理框架難以有效回應人機互動中的“黑箱决策”與責任彌散問題。本文從儒家“仁、義、禮、信”出發，提出關係性人機倫理分析框架：以“義”與“禮”明確開發者、操作者、監管者的分布式責任邊界；以“仁”與“信”論證信任不僅源於技術可靠性，更植根於人-機-機構關係中的誠意與仁心。進而提出“人技有義、人技有信”的倫理秩序，並從設計、應用、審查、監管四個層面給出實踐路徑。本文旨在為高技術醫療時代的人機關係提供植根於中華優秀傳統文化的倫理智慧，推動iPSC技術在“仁智合一”的軌道上健康發展。 The clinical application of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) increasingly depends on automated technologies, including robotic cell culture, artificial intelligence–assisted quality control, and surgical support systems. These technologies improve efficiency and precision, but they raise ethical concerns regarding the attribution of responsibility and the basis of trust in human–machine interaction. Existing human-centred ethical approaches cannot fully address black-box decision-making or the diffusion of responsibility in technologically mediated medical practice. Drawing on the Confucian concepts of ren, yi, li, and xin, this paper develops a relational framework for analysing human–machine ethics. It argues that yi and li can help define the responsibilities of developers, operators, and regulators, while ren and xin suggest that trust depends not only on technical performance but also on sincerity and benevolence in human–machine–institutional relations. On this basis, the paper proposes an eth…

title: 前言：人機關係、類器官智能、安樂死
abstract: 如何看待人機關係是當今高科技所引發的一個不可忽視的倫理問題。人際關係的核心是主體間性（intersubjectivity）與交互性（mutuality）。主體間性和交互性依賴於雙向生成內在經驗與回應，亦來源於雙向的信任與默契。然而人機關係能否等同於傳統意義上的人際關係呢？本期有三篇文章討論這個話題。 (撮要取自內文首段)

Deep learning-based body weight estimation from lower abdominal CT scans
abstract: Abstract Body weight is a key parameter for assessing the risk of an osteoporotic hip fracture by autonomous finite element analysis based on lower abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans. To allow opportunistic diagnosis of this fracture risk by any lower abdominal ? CT scan, we herein present a deep learning algorithm for estimating the patient’s body weight directly from lower abdominal CT scans. The algorithm is composed of two automatic steps: pre-processing of the CT scan followed by a two-branch convolutional neural network combining image features from axial CT slices with patient metadata. The algorithm was trained on 100 CT scans from different CT scanners and tested on 24 held-out test subjects. The body weight estimation has a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3.62 kg, and a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 4.26 kg on the 24 test set, with 75.0% of predictions within ± 5 kg and 100% within ± 10 kg of actual weight. The Pearson correlation coefficient was 0.93 (R 2 = 0.88), demonstrating a good predictive performance. To further validate these results, a five-fold cross-validation was performed, yielding an average MAE of 7.43 ± 1.14 kg and an average RMSE of 9.65 ± 1.59 kg. On average across all folds, 45.0% of predictions were within ± 5 kg and 72% were within ± 10 kg of the actual weight. This automated algorithm for determining body weight allows an opportunistic di…

title: Penggunaan Individual Learning Plan dan Arah Belajar Siswa Pendidikan Kesetaraan: Studi Eksploratif
abstract: Individual Learning Plans (ILPs) are intended to connect students’ interests, strengths, goals, and learning actions, yet evidence on how students actually use such plans remains limited, particularly in equivalency education. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined self-reported learning direction and active ILP use among 31 junior- and senior-secondary-equivalent students at PKBM Flexi School Bintaro, Indonesia. The 12-item, five-point Likert questionnaire was developed from the ILP, personalized learning, goal-setting, and self-regulated learning literature, reviewed internally by two senior facilitators for content relevance, and organized a priori into four conceptual groups—self-understanding, direction and goal clarity, planning and ILP use, and monitoring and reflection—that separate students' self-reported conditions from items explicitly referring to ILP use. Because internal consistency of the four groups was modest (α = .50–.58), reflecting the instrument's status as an initial, not-yet-validated version, item-level analysis rather than group-score comparison was treated as the primary and more trustworthy level of evidence. Self-understanding indicators received relatively higher responses, whereas indicators explicitly referring to active ILP use were weaker. The lowest item was revisiting the ILP to decide the next learning step (M = 2.84; 25.8% selected …
